SECTION-1

THE FOUNDER'S VISION
🖙 "It is my earnest hope and prayer, that this centre of life and light, which is coming into existence, will
 produce students who will not only be intellectually equal to the best of their fellow students in other parts of the world, but will also live a noble life, love their country and be loyal to the Supreme Ruler."
🖙 "A teaching university would but half perform its function, if it does not seek to develop the heart power of its scholars with the same solicitude with which it develops their brain power. Hence, this university has placed formation of character in youth as one of its principal objects. It will seek not merely to turn out men as Engineers, Scientists, Doctors, Theologists, Merchants, but also as men of high character, probity and honour, whose conduct through life would show that they bear the hallmark of a great university."

OBJECTIVES OF THE UNIVERSITY

🖙 To promote the study of the Hindu Shastras and Sanskrit literature as a means of preserving and popularizing for the benefit of the Hindus in particular and of the world at large in general.
🖙 To promote learning and research in Arts and Sciences in its branches.
🖙 To advance and diffuse such scientific, technical and professional knowledge, combined with the neces - sary practical training to promote indigenous industries and developing the material resources.
🖙 To promote the building up of character in youth by religion and ethics as an integral part of education.

THE UNIVERSITY AT A GLANCE
Banaras Hindu University (BHU), stands as one of the most prestigious and historic educational institutions in the country. Founded in 1916 by the visionary nationalist leader Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, BHU was established with the mission of promoting Indian culture, spirituality, and values through modern scientific education. Its holistic model of education, conceived and enriched by its illustrious founder, offers refreshingly new perspectives to young minds, and nurtures and facilitates their creative talents as well. This unique blend of traditional and contemporary knowledge systems has positioned BHU as a beacon of learning and enlightenment.

The sprawling campus of BHU, which stretches over 550 Hectares (1,300 acres), is a testament to its grandeur and academic excellence. Perhaps this is one of the few universities in the world where courses ranging from nursery and primary school to Doctoral/ Post-doctoral degrees are taught and pursued within a walled campus.
It enshrines within its precincts, a phenomenal range of teaching disciplines incorporating almost all conceivable subjects of Physical, Chemical & Biological Sciences, Engineering & Technology, Medical Sciences,
Humanities, Sanskrit Vidya Dharm Vigyan Social Sciences, Commerce, Law, Education, Visual Arts, Performing
Arts, Agriculture, Veterinary Sciences, Library Science, Journalism and a large number of Indian and Foreign
Languages.

The university houses 5 Institutes, 16 Faculties, 136 Departments, and the Mahila Mahavidyalaya. The Indian
Institute of Technology (BHU) is also situated on its campus. These institutions contribute to the overarching goal of the University, fostering interdisciplinary learning and research. The emphasis on research and innovation is evident from the University's state -of-the-art laboratories, libraries, and research centres, which provide students and faculty with unparalleled resources to pursue their academic interests.

The BHU has four colleges admitted to its privileges in the city. The University also runs three schools and has a Kendriya Vidyalaya within the campus. In addition, the University has its Rajiv Gandhi South Campus, spread over an area of 1092.6 Hectares (2700 acres), located about 75 km from the main campus at Barkachha in
Mirzapur district, Uttar Pradesh.

The cultural and intellectual vibrancy of BHU is reflected in its diverse student body and faculty, who come from various parts of India and the world. This melting pot of cultures and ideas creates a stimulating environment that encourages critical thinking, creativity, and holistic development. The university's

 commitment to inclusivity and diversity is further underscored by its numerous scholarships and financial aid programs, which ensure that talented students from all socioeconomic backgrounds can access quality education.

Beyond academics, BHU is celebrated for its active engagement in extracurricular activities and social initiatives. The University hosts a multitude of cultural festivals, sports events, and seminars that enrich the student experience and foster a sense of community. Additionally, outreach programs and collaborations with national and international institutions underscore the role of BHU as a catalyst for societal progress and global cooperation.

Hallmark of Excellence

The Banaras Hindu University demonstrated significant excellence during the academic session 2023-24 through its high rankings in national and international assessments, substantial research output, and robust research funding. These achievements reflect its commitment to academic excellence, impactful research, and overall contribution to various fields of study. The comprehensive accreditation and ranking information provide a testament to the institution's prestigious standing and continued dedication to fostering an environment of learning and innovation.

SECTION-2

COMMON UNIVERSITY ENTRANCE TEST (CUET) - 2026

Banaras Hindu University shall be taking admission to different programs/courses mentioned in this Bulletin based on the candidate’s merit in CUET 2026 and other program/course -specific eligibility criteria mentioned in this bulletin. The CUET - 2026 will be conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) for which the candidate is advised to visit the official website of NTA - https://cuet.nta.nic.in/ and https://cuet.nta.nic.in/registration -for-cuetug-2026-is-live/

General Instructions and Guidelines

2.1 Regular Students

Applicants must be Indian citizens to be eligible for Undergraduate Program admissions at Banaras
Hindu University.
All candidates, including those applying under the supernumerary quota, must appear for the Com - mon University Entrance Test (CUET-UG) 2026. Registration for CUET-UG 2026 is available at https://cuet.nta.nic.in/.
For seat allocation and admissions, candidates are required to apply through the Common Allotment
Program (CAP-UG 2026) of Banaras Hindu University.

2.2 Foreign Nationals

Supernumerary seats, up to 25%, in each program are reserved for foreign nationals.
Candidates under the Foreign Students category must register through the Foreign Students’ Registry only.
Foreign National Candidates, including those who have completed their previous qualifying degree from an Indian university or board, will be considered foreign candidates for admission purposes.
Such candidates will be eligible for admission under the quota designated for foreign students.
Foreign candidates seeking admission to postgraduate programs must apply through the Foreign
Students’ Registration Portal at https://bhu.ac.in.
Foreign nationals are exempted from appearing in the CUET (UG) - 2026.
Admissions under the foreign students’ category will be merit-based only.

Contact Information for Foreign Students
For assistance or inquiries regarding admission contact:

Prof. Rajesh Singh
Coordinator, International Collaborations and International Students
Mobile No.: +91-9453048443, +91-9377155303
E-mail id: int.collaboration@bhu.ac.in

2.3 Important Instructions
1. Admission Basis
Admissions to all undergraduate programs at BHU and its ‘colleges admitted to the privilege of BHU’ will be determined by scores obtained in the Common University Entrance Test (CUET-UG) 2026.
Seat allocation and admissions for all undergraduate programs (excluding Foreign Students) will be conducted through the Combined Allotment Program – Undergraduate 2026 (CAP-UG 2026). Detailed information regarding CAP -UG 2026 will be announced on the official BHU admission website at https://admission.bhu.ac.in/en. Candidates must frequently check this website for updates.

2. Pre-Registration Guidance
Before registering for CUET-UG 2026, candidates are strongly advised to carefully read the CUET-UG
Information Bulletin 2026 issued by BHU.
Candidates should also familiarize themselves with the Banaras Hindu University Act, 1916, the University Statutes (including amendments), and the Ordinances, Rules, and Regulations available on the BHU website.

3. Eligibility Criteria
Candidates must ensure they meet the Minimum Eligibility Criteria before applying.
Students appearing for their qualifying degree examination or awaiting results are eligible to appear for CUET-UG 2026 but must fulfill eligibility requirements at the time of admission.
4. Program-Specific Requirements
Candidates must meet the program-specific eligibility criteria and appear for the relevant CUET paper. Details about the syllabus are available at https://cuet.nta.nic.in/participating-universities/.
Admission is based solely on CUET-UG 2026 scores, except for programs requiring practical test or physical test.
5. Admission Responsibility
Candidates must verify their eligibility for their chosen program(s) before appearing for CUETUG 2026. Admission will only be granted if all prescribed eligibility criteria are met.
Misrepresentation of eligibility, category, or other claims will result in admission cancellation and may lead to legal action.
6. Admission Process
In addition to CUET-UG 2026, candidates must apply for BHU’s Combined Allotment Program – 2026
(CAP-UG 2026).
Certain fields (e.g., name, signature, photograph, registered email and mobile number) will auto- populate from the CUET-UG 2026 form and cannot be edited in the CAP -UG 2026 application.
7. Reservation Policies
Candidates seeking reservations under SC/ST/OBC-NCL/EWS/PwBD/SPORTS categories must upload valid certificates during the CAP-UG 2026 application.
Candidate and parent names must match those on qualifying certificates and CUET-UG 2026 records.
8. Additional Notes
Gap years will not affect eligibility for admission.
There is minimum age requirement for each program. Candidates are required to ensure it before applying.
Pursuing two regular degree programs simultaneously is not permitted.
9. Regular Updates and Notifications
Candidates must regularly check the BHU admission website (https://admission.bhu.ac.in/en) for updates and notifications. Grievances arising from unawareness of published information will not be considered.
10. Candidate Responsibilities
Candidates are required to regularly visit the NTA and BHU websites for updates related to CUET-UG
2026, seat allocation, and admission policies. Complaints arising from failure to review the bulletin or website updates will not be entertained at any stage.
This bulletin serves as a reference, compiling information from NTA, various BHU faculties, departments, and related sources. 2.6 MINIMUM ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS
1. Restrictions on Reappearing in the Entrance Test
➢ Candidates already admitted as regular students in Semester-I of any course through an entrance test in previous year, and who are eligible to appear for the 2nd-semester examination, are not permitted to reappear for the entrance test for the same course.

➢ Candidates’ ineligible for the 2nd-semester examination due to insufficient attendance or failure to submit the examination form on time may be allowed to reappear for the entrance test provided they meet the eligibility criteria.

➢ Candidates already admitted to Semester-III beyond are not allowed to take the entrance test for the same course. Violation of this rule by bonafide students will be treated as misconduct and dealt with accordingly.

2. Qualifying Examination Requirements
➢ Candidates must have passed the Class XII examination or its equivalent from a recognized board.

➢ Alternatively, candidates must have passed the Class XII examination from any Board/University in India, or a foreign institution recognized as equivalent to the 10+2 system by the Association of Indian Universities (AIU).

➢ For admission to the Banaras Hindu University, candidates are required to appear in the CUET (UG) - 2026 in the subjects they have studied and/or passed in Class XII.

➢ If grades are awarded in the qualifying examination:

Where the grade sheet does not indicate the equivalent percentage, candidate must submit a certifi - cate from the institution specifying the percentage or the formula for conversion.

If the grade sheet includes the percentage or conversion formula, candidate must provide photocopies of both sides of the degree/grade sheet.

➢ The aggregate percentage of marks includes grace marks, as reflected in the final mark sheet. For courses with different types of final mark sheets (e.g., BHU's B.A./B.Sc. Hons.), the aggregate will be calculated using the total marks for all subjects studied over all the years, rather than just honors subjects.

3. Recognition of Degrees/Certificates
➢ Only degrees/certificates recognized by the Association of Indian Universities (AIU) are considered equivalent.

➢ For distance education, recognition by the Distance Education Council of IGNOU/AIU is required. Such candidates must submit recognition/approval certificates from the IGNOU Distance Education Council.

4. Eligibility Requirements and Information Bulletin
➢ The eligibility criteria specified in the Information Bulletin and CAP-UG for the academic session are final.

5. Rejection of Fraudulent Applications
➢ Applications with forged or fraudulent certificates will be rejected, and the candidate may be barred from future entrance tests.

➢ Admission may be cancelled if the candidate fails to meet eligibility requirements, provides false documentation, or suppresses information.

6. Test Appearance
➢ Candidates must appear in the entrance test. Admission is subject to verification of qualifying mark sheets, certificates, and the absence of misconduct in previous examinations.

➢ Appearance in the test or achieving passing marks does not guarantee admission. Applicants must meet all eligibility criteria before submitting their application.

The reservations to different categories of candidates are as per the Government of India Rules and the decision of Academic and Executive Council. Reservation is available as per the following description:

Examination and appeared in the Central University Combined Entrance Test conducted by NTA.

➢ Every SC/ST candidate shall have to submit a self-attested copy of the Caste Certificate mentioning that the candidate belongs to SC/ST community. The Caste/ Tribe of the candidate must be listed in the appropriate Govt. of India schedule. Such certificates shall be subject to verification from the concerned
District Magistrate. The following are empowered to issue the certificate. Certificate from any other person/authority shall not be accepted in any case.

➢ District Magistrate/Additional District Magistrate/Collector/Deputy Commissioner/Addl. Deputy
Commissioner/ Deputy Collector/1st Class Stipendiary Magistrate/ City Magistrate/Sub-Divisional
Magistrate/Taluka Magistrate/ Executive Magistrate/Extra Assistant Commissioner.

➢ Chief Presidency Magistrate/Addl. Chief Presidency Magistrate/Presidency Magistrate.

➢ In case a SC/ST candidate seeks admission under some other category (for example,
PwBD/Employee Ward etc.) the candidate should satisfy the minimum eligibility requirement for that category.

Category of the list of Central Govt. Further the OBC certificate should clearly mention that the candidate is not under creamy layer.

2.7.5 Consideration of Reserved Category Meritorious Candidates as General Candidates

➢ In a course, if the merit of a reserved category candidate is more than or equal to the merit of the last admitted general candidate in that course, the reserved category candidate will be treated as general candidate in that course. Provided further that if a meritorious reserved category candidate is admitted by relaxing the general qualifying standards (minimum eligibility requirement and/or age) or is admitted to a higher preferred course (allotment of Honours subject, Major Minor combination, Specialization, if any) which he/she would not have got by remaining under the general category, then his/her admission shall be adjusted against the concerned reserved category quota and the consequential vacancy created in the general category shall be filled up by a general category candidate in order of merit.

2.9 INTER-SE RANKING - Breaking Ties in CUET (UG) - 2026 Merit Scores
In case of a tie, where two or more candidates have the same CUET(UG)-2026 merit score for a Program
+ Faculty/College Combination, the tie -breaking rules will be applied in the following sequence:

1) Preference shall be given to the candidates who have a higher aggregate percentage of marks at the Qualifying Examination.
2) However, in cases for admission to B.Sc. and B.Sc. (Hons.) Ag., the aggregate marks in Science subjects shall only be considered for this purpose.
3) Even, if case tie, then Preference will be given to candidates with higher aggregate percentages in the best three/four/five Class XII subjects.
4) In case the candidates have equal marks in the above-stated Examinations, then the candidate senior in age shall be given preference.

Agricultural Science is an interdisciplinary field that builds on strong foundations in Agriculture, Food and Dairy.
It focuses on studying the structure and function of various biological components within plants, animals, and microorganisms, as well as their complex interactions that sustain agricultural ecosystems. The scope of
Agricultural Science as an interdisciplinary subject is vast, encompassing aspects of crop and soil science, plant and animal physiology, and sustainable farming practices. FACULTY OF SOCIAL SCIENCES

1. (UG0132) Bachelor of Arts in Economics/ Geography/ History / Political Science/ Psychology/
Sociology - Under NEP Curriculum
A B.A. in Economics provides analytical skills for understanding markets, policies, and financial systems. It offers careers in banking, policy-making, business, and research, enhancing problem-solving and data analysis abilities.
A B.A. in Geography develops spatial analysis skills, understanding of environmental systems, and urban planning.
It leads to careers in GIS, cartography, climate research, and sustainable development, aiding policy decisions and resource management. A B.A. in History enhances critical thinking, research, and analytical skills by studying past events. It supports careers in education, archiving, journalism, and public administration, fostering a deeper understanding of societal evolution. A B.A. in Political Science provides knowledge of governance, law, and international relations. It opens career paths in public service, diplomacy, policy analysis, and journalism, enhancing leadership, communication, and decision-making skills. A B.A. in Psychology offers insights into human behavior, cognition, and mental health. It supports careers in counseling, HR, research, and social work, improving interpersonal skills and problem-solving abilities. A B.A. in Sociology studies social structures, culture, and human interactions. It prepares students for careers in social work, research, public policy, and community development, enhancing analytical and communication skills.

Eligibility for Admission
Passed 10+2 or equivalent examination securing a minimum of 50% marks in the aggregate.
For B.A. Major/Minor in Economics, the candidate must have studied Mathematics as subject at High School
Examination.

FACULTY OF SANSKRIT VIDYA DHARMA VIJNANA

1. (UG0187) Shastri - Under NEP Curriculum

A Shashtri in Shukla Yajurveda and Krishna Yajurveda gains deep knowledge of Vedic rituals, yajnas, and spiritual philosophy. Expertise in Vyakaran (grammar) and Sahitya (literature) enhances linguistic precision and scriptural interpretation. Jyotish Ganit and Jyotish Falit provide insights into mathematical astrology and predictive sciences.
Sankhyayoga and Nyay-Vaisheshika develop logical reasoning and metaphysical understanding, while Vedant explores ultimate reality. Puranetihas and Dharmashastra offer historical and ethical perspectives. Mimansa and
Dharmagam refine ritualistic analysis. Comparative studies in Jain Darshan and Bauddha Darshan enrich philosophical discourse. This knowledge benefits scholars, priests, astrologers, and philosophers in spiritual and academic pursuits.

Eligibility for Admission
Passed Madhyama Examination of BHU/Madhyama/Uttar Madhyama/Upa Shastri/Intermediate or 10+2 or equivalent with a minimum 50% marks in the aggregate. Sanskrit must be one of the subjects in the concerned examination and candidate should have passed in this subject also.
The candidates having passed one year certificate course in Sanskrit of BHU after passing 10+2 examination with
50% marks in aggregate both in 10+2 examination and certificate examination are also eligible.
AGE: Not to be more than 22 years on 1st July 2026.

FACULTY OF VISUAL ARTS

1. (UG0180) Bachelor of Fine Arts in Applied Arts/Painting/Plastic Art/ Pottery & Ceramics/ Textile
Design - Under NEP Curriculum

Applied Arts offer numerous advantages across various disciplines. Painting enhances creativity and visual storytelling, serving both aesthetic and commercial purposes. Textile Design combines art with functionality, influencing fashion, interiors, and industrial fabrics. Plastic Arts (sculpture, installation, and mixed media) provide three-dimensional artistic expression, enriching public spaces and galleries. Pottery & Ceramics merge tradition with innovation, producing functional and decorative items while preserving cultural heritage. These fields contribute to design, industry, and daily life, fostering artistic expression, innovation, and economic opportunities. Applied Arts bridge creativity with utility, making art accessible and integral to various sectors, from fashion to home decor.

                                                      THE UNIVERSITY AT A GLANCE
         Banaras Hindu University (BHU), stands as one of the most prestigious and historic educational institutions in
         the country. Founded in 1916 by the visionary nationalist leader Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, BHU was
         established with the mission of promoting Indian culture, spirituality, and values through modern scientific
         education. Its holistic model of education, conceived and enriched by its illustrious founder, offers refreshingly
         new perspectives to young minds, and nurtures and facilitates their creative talents as well. This unique blend
         of  traditional  and  contemporary  knowledge  systems  has  positioned  BHU  as  a  beacon  of  learning  and
         enlightenment.

         The sprawling campus of BHU, which stretches over 550 Hectares (1,300 acres), is a testament to its grandeur
         and academic excellence. Perhaps this is one of the few universities in the world where courses ranging from
         nursery and primary school to Doctoral/ Post-doctoral degrees are                  taught and pursued within a walled campus.
         It  enshrines  within  its  precincts,  a  phenomenal  range  of  teaching  disciplines  incorporating  almost  all
         conceivable subjects of Physical, Chemical & Biological Sciences, Engineering & Technology, Medical Sciences,
         Humanities, Sanskrit Vidya Dharm Vigyan Social Sciences,                 Commerce, Law, Education, Visual Arts, Performing
         Arts, Agriculture, Veterinary Sciences, Library Science, Journalism and a large number of Indian and Foreign
         Languages.

         The university houses 5 Institutes, 16 Faculties, 136 Departments, and the Mahila Mahavidyalaya. The Indian
         Institute of Technology (BHU) is also situated on its campus. These institutions contribute to the overarching
         goal  of  the  University,  fostering  interdisciplinary  learning  and  research.  The  emphasis  on  research  and
         innovation is evident from the University's state           -of-the-art laboratories, libraries, and research centres, which
         provide students and faculty with unparalleled resources to pursue their academic interests.

         The BHU has four colleges admitted to its privileges in the city. The University also runs three schools                        and has
         a Kendriya Vidyalaya within the campus. In addition, the University has its Rajiv Gandhi South Campus, spread
         over an area of 1092.6 Hectares (2700 acres), located about 75 km from the main campus at Barkachha in
         Mirzapur district, Uttar Pradesh.

         The cultural and intellectual vibrancy of BHU is reflected in its diverse student body and faculty, who come
         from various parts of India and the world. This melting pot of cultures and ideas creates a stimulating

THE FOUNDER'S VISION

🖙 "It is my earnest hope and prayer, that this centre of life and light, which is coming into existence, will produce students who will not only be intellectually equal to the best of their fellow students in other parts of the world, but will also live a noble life, love their country and be loyal to the Supreme Ruler."
🖙 "A teaching university would but half perform its function, if it does not seek to develop the heart power of its scholars with the same solicitude with which it develops their brain power. Hence, this university has placed formation of character in youth as one of its principal objects. It will seek not merely to turn out men as
Engineers, Scientists, Doctors, Theologists, Merchants, but also as men of high character, probity and honour, whose conduct through life would show that they bear the hallmark of a great university."

OBJECTIVES OF THE UNIVERSITY

🖙 To promote the study of the Hindu Shastras and Sanskrit literature as a means of preserving and popularizing for the benefit of the Hindus in particular and of the world at large in general.
🖙 To promote learning and research in Arts and Sciences in its branches.
🖙 To advance and diffuse such scientific, technical and professional knowledge, combined with the necessary practical training to promote indigenous industries and developing the material resources.
🖙 To promote the building up of character in youth by religion and ethics as an integral part of education.

THE UNIVERSITY AT A GLANCE
Banaras Hindu University (BHU), stands as one of the most prestigious and historic educational institutions in the country. Founded in 1916 by the visionary nationalist leader Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, BHU was established with the mission of promoting Indian culture, spirituality, and values through modern scientific education. Its holistic model of education, conceived and enriched by its illustrious founder, offers refreshingly new perspectives to young minds, and nurtures and facilitates their creative talents as well. This unique blend of traditional and contemporary knowledge systems has positioned BHU as a beacon of learning and enlightenment.

The sprawling campus of BHU, which stretches over 550 Hectares (1,300 acres), is a testament to its grandeur and academic excellence. Perhaps this is one of the few universities in the world where courses ranging from nursery and primary school to Doctoral/ Post-doctoral degrees are taught and pursued within a walled campus.
It enshrines within its precincts, a phenomenal range of teaching disciplines incorporating almost all conceivable subjects of Physical, Chemical & Biological Sciences, Engineering & Technology, Medical Sciences, Humanities,
Sanskrit Vidya Dharm Vigyan Social Sciences, Commerce, Law, Education, Visual Arts, Performing Arts,
Agriculture, Veterinary Sciences, Library Science, Journalism and a large number of Indian and Foreign
Languages.

The university houses 5 Institutes, 16 Faculties, 136 Departments, and the Mahila Mahavidyalaya. The Indian
Institute of Technology (BHU) is also situated on its campus. These institutions contribute to overarching goal of the University, fostering interdisciplinary learning and research. The emphasis on research and innovation is evident from the state-of-the-art laboratories, libraries, and research centres of the University, which provide students and faculty with unparalleled resources to pursue their academic interests.

The BHU has four colleges admitted to its privileges in the city. The University also runs three schools apart from having a Kendriya Vidyalaya within the campus. In addition, the University has its South Campus spread over an area of 1092.6 Hectares (2700 acres) located about 75 kms from the main campus, at Barkachha in Mirzapur district, Uttar Pradesh.

The cultural and intellectual vibrancy of BHU is reflected in its diverse student body and faculty, who come from various parts of India and the world. This melting pot of cultures and ideas creates a stimulating environment that encourages critical thinking, creativity, and holistic development. The university's commitment to inclusivity and diversity is further underscored by its numerous scholarships and financial aid programs, which ensure that talented students from all socioeconomic backgrounds can access quality education.

Beyond academics, BHU is celebrated for its active engagement in extracurricular activities and social initiatives.
The University hosts a multitude of cultural festivals, sports events, and seminars that enrich the student experience and foster a sense of community. Additionally, outreach programs and collaborations with national and international institutions underscore the role of BHU as a catalyst for societal progress and global cooperation.

Hallmark of Excellence

The Banaras Hindu University demonstrated significant excellence during the academic session 2024-25 through its high rankings in national and international assessments, substantial research output, and robust research funding. These achievements reflect its commitment to academic excellence, impactful research, and overall contribution to various fields of study. The comprehensive accreditation and ranking information provide a testament to the institution's prestigious standing and continued dedication to fostering an environment of learning and innovation.

Largest Residential University in Asia

Over 38,000 students from all over India and abroad are enrolled in various courses in the distinct Faculties of the University. The University has 72 hostels, accommodating nearly 11000 inmates, with all modern amenities

 including internet for the students. It also has 1667 staff quarters and 5guesthouses on campus. Besides, the
University houses several independent autonomous institutions within its campus.

Shri Vishwanath Temple

The Banaras Hindu University has a temple of Lord Shiva called Shri Vishwanath Temple. The temple is built with white marble, is one of the highlights of Varanasi situated at the centre of the campus. Its detailed planning was done by Malaviya Ji himself. The lush campus of Shri
Vishwanath Temple and the beautiful gardens surrounding it are a delight to the eyes of the visitors. The interior of the temple has a Shiva Lingam and verses from Hindu scriptures inscribed on the walls of the temple with pictorial depictions.

Institution of Eminence (IoE)

Banaras Hindu University has been bestowed with the prestigious tag of Institution of Eminence by the Government of India. Under the scheme, the University is being provided a grant of Rs.
1,000 Crore over a period of 5 years, for achieving excellence in teaching and research, to inspire holistic values of development and sustainability.

BHU Alumni

The contribution of BHU in extending the frontiers of knowledge in critical areas and the regeneration and efflorescence of community values is well manifested through its extensive alumni network, which is constitutive of distinguished personalities throughout the world occupying key positions in varied professional domains.

2.3 NOTES ON MINIMUM ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS

Restrictions on Reappearing in the Entrance Test:

⮚ Candidates already admitted as regular students in Semester-I of any course through an entrance test in previous years, and who are eligible to appear for the 2nd-semester examination, are not permitted to reappear for the entrance test for the same course.

⮚ Candidates ineligible for the 2nd-semester examination due to insufficient attendance or failure to submit the examination form on time may be allowed to reappear for the entrance test, provided they meet the eligibility criteria.

⮚ Candidates already admitted to Semester-III beyond are not allowed to take the entrance test for the same course. Violations of this rule by bonafide students will be treated as misconduct and dealt with accordingly.

Qualifying Examination Requirements:

⮚ If grades are awarded in the qualifying examination:

⮲ Where the grade sheet does not indicate the equivalent percentage, candidates must submit a certificate from the institution specifying the percentage or the formula for conversion.

⮲ If the grade sheet includes the percentage or conversion formula, candidates must provide photocopies of both sides of the degree/grade sheet.

⮚ The aggregate percentage of marks includes grace marks, as reflected in the final mark sheet. For courses with different types of final mark sheets (e.g., BHU's B.A./B.Sc. Honours), the aggregate will be

 calculated using the total marks for all subjects studied over all the years, rather than just honors subjects.

Recognition of Degrees/Certificates:

⮚ Only degrees/certificates recognized by the Association of Indian Universities (AIU) are considered equivalent.

⮚ For distance education, recognition by the Distance Education Council of IGNOU/AIU is required.
Such candidates must submit recognition/approval certificates from the IGNOU Distance Education
Council.

Eligibility Requirements and Information Bulletin:

⮚ The eligibility criteria specified in the Information Bulletin and CAP-PG for the academic session are final.

Rejection of Fraudulent Applications:

⮚ Applications with forged or fraudulent certificates will be rejected, and the candidate may be barred from future entrance tests.

⮚ Admission may be canceled if the candidate fails to meet eligibility requirements, provides false documentation, or suppresses information.

Provisional Test Appearance:

⮚ Candidates may take the entrance test provisionally. Admission is subject to verification of qualifying mark sheets, certificates, and the absence of misconduct in previous university examinations.

⮚ Appearance in the test or achieving passing marks does not guarantee admission. Applicants must meet all eligibility criteria before submitting their application.

2.7 INTER-SE RANKING: Breaking Ties in CUET (PG) - 2026 Merit Scores:

In case of equal RANK in CUET-PG (for all courses), the following criteria shall be adopted for inter -se ranking,
If two or more candidates have the same score for a program in the CUET (PG) - 2026, the following criteria will be used in a stated order to break the tie:

1. Qualifying Exam Performance: The candidate with the highest marks in the qualifying degree examination shall be given preference. Provided that in case of those students whose final semester/year results have not been declared, the qualifying degree examination percentage shall include marks obtained till last semesters.
2. If the tie persists, the candidate with the higher marks in their last available semester/year final year of the qualifying degree will be considered. If a tie remains, the process will move to considering marks in the preceding semesters (or years) until the tie is broken.
3. Age: If the tie remains, the older candidate (based on their Class X certificate date of birth) will be given preference.
4. Application Number: If all else is equal, Application number of the candidate; preference will be given to the candidate who applied earlier in the CAP -PG 2026.

Additional Tie-Breaking Rules (For All Courses):

1. In rare cases where a tie persists across all programs a candidate applied for; these additional criteria will be used: Subject-Specific Marks (if applicable):

2. If overall qualifying exam marks are also equal, the candidate with higher marks in the relevant subject of the program will be chosen. (For MCA programs, if overall marks are equal, candidates with a Bachelor's degree in Mathematics will be considered first. Further tie-breaking will be based on Mathematics marks in
Bachelor's, then Intermediate (+2), and lastly, for those with Mathematics only in +2.

3. Preference shall be given to the candidates who have higher aggregate percentage of marks at the Qualifying
Examination. (in cases where candidates with graduation/post-graduation such as M.A. in Linguistics and
M.A. in Mass Communication are eligible, the inter-se-ranking will be decided on the basis of percentage of marks in aggregate at graduation level)

4. In case the aggregate percentages of the marks at the Qualifying Examination are also equal then preference shall be given to a candidate who has higher marks in the concerned subject (wherever applicable). In MCA:
In case the aggregate percentages of the marks at qualifying examination are also equal, then the candidates having Mathematics at Bachelor’s level shall be considered first. If there are several such candidates, then preference shall be given to a candidate who has higher percentage of marks in Mathematics at Bachelor’s level, and if these are also equal, then at Intermediate or +2 level. Lastly, candidates having Mathematics at +2 level but not at Bachelor’s level will be considered similarly.

3.1 INSTITUTE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES

The Institute of Agricultural Sciences (I.Ag.Sc.) at Banaras Hindu University has concluded a distinguished journey spanning 93 years, marked by substantial contributions towards alleviating hunger in India. Initially established under various names, it was formally designated as the Institute of Agricultural Sciences in 1981, with a mission to integrate education, research, extension services, and agricultural development. Pioneering as the first Institute of Agricultural Research offering M.Sc. and Ph.D. degrees, it commenced undergraduate education in 1945 under the title of the College of Agriculture within the Faculty of Engineering. This college attained independent status as the Faculty of Agriculture in 1968.

Presently, the Institute comprises two faculties: the Faculty of Agriculture and the Faculty of Veterinary and
Animal Sciences, encompassing 11 and 15 departments respectively along with three auxiliary units. It currently provides comprehensive education and involved in research across diverse fields of Agriculture and Veterinary
Sciences, offering programs such as B.Sc. (Ag.), 02 B.Tech. (DT & FT) programs, 11 M.Sc. (Ag.) programs, 02
M.Tech ( DT & FPT) programs, B.V.Sc. & A.H., and Ph.D. programs.

The academic year 2023-24 marked a period of substantial achievement and growth for the institute, characterized by robust research outputs, strategic collaborations, infrastructure development, and comprehensive student development initiatives. These accomplishments underscore the commitment of the
Institute to excellence in education, research, and community engagement, positioning it as a leader in agricultural and allied sciences.

3.2 INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCES

The Institute of Medical Sciences (IMS), a distinguished constituent of Banaras Hindu University, stands as a premier medical institution in India, notable for its four comprehensive faculties: the Faculty of Medicine, comprising 35 departments; the Faculty of Ayurveda, with 17 departments; the Faculty of Dental Sciences; and the College of Nursing. In addition to these faculties, the Institute operates several constituent hospitals, offering a total of 2,614 beds, including 1,385 in Sir Sunderlal Hospital, 180 in the Ayurveda Wing, 334 in the Trauma
Centre, 13 in the Faculty of Dental Sciences, 430 in the Centenary Super Specialty Block, 100 in the Mother &
Child Health Wing, 60 in the Centre of Excellence for Mental Health, 12 in the Bone Marrow Transplant & Stem
Cell Research Centre, and 100 in the Regional Institute of Ophthalmology. IMS also houses a Regional Resource
Centre for Telemedicine, providing state-of-the-art tele-education and tele-consultation facilities with high-tech classrooms.

The Institute offers comprehensive academic programs in medicine, including undergraduate (UG), postgraduate
(PG), post-doctoral (D.M. and M.Ch.), and Ph.D. degrees, fostering cutting-edge research, clinical training, and medical practice in a wide array of disciplines.

Hospitals and Clinical Facilities

With 1,585 beds in Sir Sunderlal Hospital and 334 beds in the Trauma Centre, IMS extends world-class healthcare services to economically disadvantaged populations from Eastern Uttar Pradesh, seven neighbouring states, and even the adjoining country of Nepal. In addition to these facilities, IMS maintains a Staff Health Centre and a
Student Health Care Complex, ensuring quality medical services for the staff and students of the University.

IMS is currently undergoing a major transformation, aspiring to become an institution of excellence akin to the
All-India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS). As part of this upgrade, a 430 -bed Centenary Super -Specialty
Block has been established, offering highly advanced and specialized medical care. This state -ofthe-art facility is equipped with 13 modular operating theatres, 50 Intensive Care Units (ICUs), and 19 Critical Care Units
(CCUs), covering 11 major super -specialty disciplines. The block also features a modern blood bank with component separation facilities, which has received an 'A' grade rating from NACO, New Delhi. A mobile blood bank van further enhances patient care services.

Additionally, several new healthcare facilities have been inaugurated, including a 100 -bed Mother and Child
Health Wing, a 100 -bed Regional Institute of Ophthalmology, a 12 -bed Bone Marrow Transplant & Stem Cell
Research Centre, and a 60-bed Centre of Excellence for Mental Health. These units, inaugurated by Honourable
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, are now fully operational.

Trauma Centre

The Trauma Centre of IMS is the largest of its kind in India, housing 334 beds, including a 27-bed modern ICU.
The facility is centrally air-conditioned and equipped with centralized gas and vacuum distribution, supported by a 10,000-liter liquid oxygen plant. The centre features 13 modular operating theatres, as well as extensive

 outpatient (Orthopaedics, Plastic Surgery, Neurosurgery) and inpatient (Neurosurgery, Orthopaedics, Plastic
Surgery, Polytrauma, and Emergency) services. It operates 24-hour emergency services, staffed with Advanced
Trauma Life Support (ATLS) and Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support (ACLS)trained personnel and equipped with advanced resuscitation tools. Furthermore, the Trauma Centre offers round-the-clock imaging services, including a 128-slice CT scanner, a 1.5 Tesla MRI machine, ultrasonography (USG), and X -ray facilities. The
Centre also boasts a blood bank, a 225-seat auditorium for academic activities, and 24-hour ambulance services, ensuring comprehensive care for trauma patients

3.3 INSTITUTE OF ENVIRONMENT & SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT

In alignment with the United Nations' vision that higher education should play a pivotal role in fostering the knowledge and competencies essential for sustainable development, Banaras Hindu University established the
Institute of Environment & Sustainable Development in 2010. This Institute is dedicated to advancing education in sustainable development, conducting research, and extending services crucial to the sustainable progress of
India, ultimately aspiring to eradicate poverty through the judicious and equitable management of the nation’s natural resources.

The Institute stands as a beacon of interdisciplinary education in the realms of environment and sustainable development. It offers a Master of Science program in Environmental Sciences, with specializations in
Environmental Biotechnology, Ecological Sciences, and Earth and Atmospheric Sciences, in addition to hosting doctoral and integrated M.Phil.-Ph.D. programs in various branches of Environmental Sciences and Technology.
These include, but are not limited to, Earth and Atmospheric Sciences, Ecological Sciences, Environmental
Microbiology, and Sustainable Agriculture. The Institute also houses the DST-Mahamana Centre of Excellence in
Climate Change, an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary collaborative research initiative aligned with India’s
National Action Plan on Climate Change.

Beyond its primary mission of teaching and research at the Institute, faculty members contribute to the academic community by participating in teaching and mentoring students across various M.Sc. programs, including
Geophysics, Environmental Sciences, Environmental Sciences & Technology, and Applied Microbiology, both at
Banaras Hindu University and other national and international institutions.

The academic year 2023-24 was a time of significant progress and accomplishment for the institute, highlighted by strong research contributions, strategic partnerships, advancements in infrastructure, and holistic student development programs. These achievements reflect the unwavering dedication of the Institute to excellence in education, research, and community involvement, solidifying its position as a leader in environmental and allied sciences.

3.4 INSTITUTE OF MANAGEMENT STUDIES

Banaras Hindu University reached a significant milestone in fulfilling the visionary aspirations of its illustrious founder by introducing postgraduate and doctoral programs in Management in 1968, establishing a new
Department within the Faculty of Commerce. Recognizing the growing demand for high-calibre management education and research, the University elevated the Department of Management Studies to an independent
Faculty of Management Studies in 1984. This transformation enabled the institution to offer innovative, industryrelevant programs, guided by distinguished faculty members of national and international repute. Further advancing its commitment to excellence, the Faculty was upgraded to the Institute of Management Studies in
December 2015.

The Institute now offers a comprehensive suite of academic programs, including the MBA, MBA -IB, MBA
(Agribusiness),

Ph.D. in Management Studies, as well as various diploma and certificate programs. The Institute maintains robust connections with the corporate sector, with academic collaborations and Guest lectures from industry experts play a crucial role in enhancing the teaching-learning experience. These interactions, along with valuable insights from industry leaders, inform the curriculum revision process, ensuring that the programs remain relevant and cutting-edge.

Moreover, the Institute houses a Business Clinic, designed to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application. The Clinic extends learning beyond the classroom, offering expert services to entrepreneurs and business entities.

The Atal Incubation Centre —Mahamana Foundation for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (AIC -MFIE-IM-BHU) operates within the Institute of Management Studies. As one of the flagship initiatives under the Atal Innovation
Mission, supported by NITI Aayog, Government of India, this Centre fosters innovative startups, guiding them towards becoming scalable and sustainable enterprises.

The academic year 2023-24 was a period of substantial achievement for the Institute of Management Studies
(IMS) at BHU. The institute demonstrated excellence in various domains, including research, strategic collaborations, infrastructure development, student -centric activities, and placement outcomes. These accomplishments reflect the unwavering commitment of the Institute to quality education, innovation, and community engagement, further solidifying its status as a leading institution in management studies.

3.5 INSTITUTE OF SCIENCE - FACULTY OF SCIENCE

Established in 1916, the Faculty of Science at Banaras Hindu University was elevated to the status of the Institute of Science, distinguishing itself as one of the premier institutions within the University. The Institute offers a comprehensive range of undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs, alongside several diploma and certificate courses. It encompasses 13 departments, 6 centres, and 2 interdisciplinary schools, all of which are equipped with state-of the-art laboratories and research facilities. The Institute continues to advance its pursuit of excellence in teaching, learning, and research across virtually all areas of basic and applied sciences.

The faculty members of the Institute maintain numerous collaborations with prestigious academic and research institutions both in India and abroad. Many of its esteemed faculty are recognized with various honours and distinctions and are fellows of several leading science academies in India.

The Institute of Science has been getting financial support from different schemes of Government of India which include DST-FIST, DRS-SAP, DST-PURSE etc. This helped the Institute to create state -of-the-art infrastructure for teaching and research. To further support and enhance research endeavours, the Institute has made significant efforts to establish new cutting-edge facilities. These include the Central Discovery Centre, SATHI
Centre, BIRAC-supported Bio-incubation setup BIONEST, Seismic Imaging Centre, among others.

Besides demonstrating remarkable academic pursuit, technological innovations and collaborations, the Institute of Science has contributed immensely towards extracurricular and student-centric activities. These achievements exemplify the steadfast dedication of the Institute to excellence in education, innovation, and community engagement, thereby reaffirming its distinguished position as a premier institution in the field of basic and applied science.

Madan Mohan Malaviya Ji’s vision for the empowerment of women through education in such a manner that our students are a perfect blend of tradition and modernity. This institution, for more than nine decades, has provided female students from diverse backgrounds the opportunity to pursue undergraduate courses in 31 subjects from different streams like Arts, Science, and Social Sciences, as well as postgraduate courses in Home Science, Education and

Bioinformatics.

MMV has nearly 2500 students from within India and all over the world who are realizing their academic potential supported by a strong infrastructure consisting of well -equipped science laboratories, a central instrumentation laboratory, a rich library, smart classrooms, six hostels, and large sports ground to mention a few.

There are more than a hundred faculty members in MMV who are contributing to the academic life of the university in various ways. This includes postgraduate teaching in the parent departments, as well as membership of the board of studies and departmental research committees. MMV faculty members are also guiding doctoral research candidates in their respective parent departments.

MMV, in keeping with the student-centric approach of the university, places great emphasis on the holistic development of its students. This is ensured through myriad programs like nurturing effective leadership through
FLY, student wellbeing initiatives, counselling and sports facilities.

During the academic year 2023-24, the Mahila Mahavidyalaya has made significant academic achievements, infrastructure developments, and active student engagement through various programs and initiatives, which shows its commitment to research, collaboration, faculty development, and student engagement through a wide range of activities.

5.1 FACULTY OF ARTS

The Faculty of Arts at Banaras Hindu University, originally established as a center of humanities, traces its roots to the Central Hindu College, founded by Dr. Annie Besant in 1898. This institution laid the groundwork for what would become the prestigious Banaras Hindu University (BHU), a beacon of academic excellence with a promising future. The Faculty is envisioned as a hub for preserving and promoting the rich intellectual and cultural heritage of India, fostering a harmonious blend of traditional and modern knowledge systems.

The Faculty of Arts continually strives to nurture a unique symbiosis between time honoured wisdom and contemporary ideas, with the goal of advancing the holistic development of humanity. It maintains a dynamic academic environment that encourages interdisciplinary research and innovation, all while upholding the principles of human liberty. Through its 21 departments and 4 significant research centers, the Faculty promotes rigorous dialogues on traditional and indigenous knowledge systems, evaluating their relevance and significance in today's world.

The Faculty offers a comprehensive range of undergraduate, postgraduate, and research programs in disciplines such as Indian and foreign languages, history, culture, archaeology, art history, and philosophy and religion.
Additionally, it provides a variety of professional and vocational courses, including Journalism and Mass
Communication, Library and Information Science, Tourism and Travel Management, Museology, and Functional
Hindi. With its B.A., M.A. programs in 21 disciplines, Ph.D. opportunities, and a wide array of diploma and certificate courses, the Faculty is dedicated to shaping informed and culturally aware citizens capable of contributing meaningfully to society.

The Faculty of Arts at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) has showcased an impressive range of academic achievements, research initiatives, and extracurricular activities during the academic year 2023 -2024.

5.2 FACULTY OF COMMERCE

The Faculty of Commerce at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) is recognized as one of the largest commerce faculties in India, with a rich history dating back to 1940. Initially established as an adjunct department to the
Department of Economics, it gained independence during the University’s Silver Jubilee celebrations in 1950 and was later elevated to the status of a full-fledged faculty in 1965.

In the current academic year, the Faculty of Commerce at BHU continues to provide a diverse array of programs, including B.Com. (Honours), M.Com., and Ph.D. courses. Additionally, it offers specialized programs such as the
M.B.A. in Financial Management (M.B.A. -F.M.), M.B.A. in Risk & Insurance (M.B.A. -R&I), and M.B.A. in Foreign
Trade (M.B.A. -F.T.) on a self -financing basis, catering to the evolving needs of the business world.

The Faculty's reach extends to the Rajiv Gandhi South Campus (RGSC) in Barkachha, Mirzapur, where it offers
B.Com. (Honours) under a paid seat category and B.Com. (Honours) in Financial Market Management (F.M.M.).
This expansion provides students in the region with opportunities for specialized education in commerce and finance.

The faculty’s accomplishments during this period illustrate its active engagement in research, publication, and academic collaboration. The contributions in research publications, book authorship, and chapter writing have enriched the academic landscape, while active participation in conferences and seminars has helped to further the exchange of knowledge. These achievements highlight the Faculty’s ongoing commitment to academic excellence and its role as a vital contributor to scholarly advancements at both national and international levels.

5.3 FACULTY OF EDUCATION

Faculty of Education, Banaras Hindu University is committed to promote education by providing educators with the tools and strategies needed to teach all learners, regardless of their abilities, and integrating inclusive education practices within the broader educational framework. The faculty encourages innovation by fostering the development and application of advanced teaching strategies, digital technologies, and inclusive curricula that cater to the needs of all students. With a focus on research excellence, the faculty leads pioneering research in all areas of education, contributing to the academic and practical knowledge required to enhance educational practices in diverse classrooms. Additionally, the Faculty aims to develop strong leadership in education, preparing future leaders who are equipped to manage educational institutions, advocate for inclusive policies, and drive reforms that will transform the education sector.

Program Offered:
The faculty of Education has six programme in the area of education and special education. The B.Ed. (Bachelor of Education), M.Ed. (Master of Education) and M.A. (Master of Arts in Education) programs at Banaras Hindu
University (BHU) are recognized by the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE). NCTE is the national regulatory body for teacher education in India, ensuring that the curriculum, teaching methods, and faculty standards meet the requirements for quality education and professional development of educators. In addition, the B.Ed. in Special Education (Hearing Impairment and Visual Impairment) and M.Ed. Special Education (Visual
Impairment) programs are recognized by the Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI), New Delhi ensuring that the programs align with the standards for special education and equip graduates to work effectively with students with disabilities, particularly those with hearing and visual impairments.
⮲ B.Ed. (Bachelor of Education): A comprehensive program preparing educators for diverse educational environments with a focus on teaching practices.
⮲ M.Ed. (Master of Education): A program designed to deepen the knowledge and skills of educators in teaching, leadership, curriculum design, and educational research.
⮲ M.A. Education (Master of Arts in Education): A program designed to deepen the knowledge and skills of educators in teaching, leadership, curriculum design, and educational research.
⮲ B.Ed. (Special Education - Hearing Impairment): A specialized undergraduate program designed to prepare teachers to work effectively with students who have hearing impairments. Emphasizes inclusive teaching, assistive technology, and rehabilitative practices.
⮲ B.Ed. (Special Education - Visual Impairment): A specialized undergraduate program designed to prepare teachers to work effectively with students who have visual impairments. Emphasizes inclusive teaching, assistive technology, and rehabilitative practices.
⮲ M.Ed. (Special Education - Visual Impairment): A program tailored for individuals seeking specialized training in the education of students with visual impairments. Focuses on rehabilitation, advocacy, and inclusive education strategies.

SECTION 6

FACULTY OF LAW

Since its inception, the Faculty of Law at Banaras Hindu University has played a pivotal role in transforming legal education and making it socially relevant. Its primary focus has been to offer career oriented legal training that equips students to meet the evolving challenges in legal education while addressing the growing demand for law graduates in sectors such as business, industry, commerce, and other emerging fields.

The Faculty has been at the forefront of legal education innovation, introducing the three -year LL.B. program, the two-year LL.M. program, and a specialized two -year LL.M. course in Human Rights and Duties Education.
Additionally, it has implemented a choice -based credit system for its LL.B. (Honours), LL.M., and LL.M. (HRDE) programs. Since 1978, the Faculty has also provided legal aid and services to marginalized and disadvantaged communities.

Presently, the Faculty offers a wide range of academic programs, including LL.B., LL.M., LL.M. (HRDE), B.A. -
LL.B., and Ph.D., along with several diploma courses. It also publishes the prestigious Banaras Law Journal, which features research articles and book reviews contributed by distinguished scholars, legal professionals, and academics. The journal is frequently cited by research scholars, as well as judges of the High Courts and the
Supreme Court of India.

The Faculty of Law at Banaras Hindu University continues to uphold its esteemed legacy through various academic, extracurricular, and student -centric initiatives. The department has demonstrated significant accomplishments across multiple domains, including research, academic events, and student development activities.

SECTION 7

FACULTY OF PERFORMING ARTS

The Faculty of Performing Arts at Banaras Hindu University is dedicated to the promotion and preservation of
India’s rich traditions in music and dance. Established in 1950, through the tireless efforts of Pt. Govind Malaviya and founding Principal Sangit Martand Pt. Omkar Nath Thakur, the College of Music and Fine Arts holds the unique distinction of founding the first Department of Musicology in India. The Faculty comprises four departments: Vocal, Instrumental, Dance, and Musicology. It offers a wide range of academic programs, including Ph.D., postgraduate,
 undergraduate, and diploma courses in both Hindustani and Karnatic vocal music, instrumental music (sitar, violin, flute, tabla and mridangam), and classical dance forms such as Kathak and Bharatnatyam.

In addition to teaching and research, faculty members and students actively participate in staging performances at government events, cultural festivals, and radio and television programs. The Faculty offers B.Mus. and M.A.
programs in three disciplines, along with Ph.D. programs, while also providing several diploma courses.

The Faculty of Performing Arts continues to stand as a beacon of excellence in the fields of music and dance.
With its strong academic framework, active involvement in national and international performances, and focus on student development and community outreach, during academic session 2023-24, the Faculty contributed significantly to the preservation and promotion of India’s cultural heritage. Through its diverse programs and initiatives, it remains at the forefront of fostering the next generation of artists and scholars.

SECTION -8

FACULTY OF SANSKRIT VIDYA DHARMA VIJNANA

The Faculty of Sanskrit Vidya Dharm Vigyan, established in 1918, was founded with the dual purpose of preserving and advancing the study of ancient Indian scriptures, Sanskrit language, and literature, while fostering a meaningful dialogue between Eastern and Western traditions. Initially known as the Faculty of Prachya Vidya, one of its primary aims is to challenge and dispel unfounded misconceptions surrounding Hindu religion, spirituality, astrology, and Tantra. It is equally dedicated to restoring the fundamental values of morality and religion, contributing to the upliftment of society at large and particularly focusing on the well -being of the masses. The Faculty preserves traditional methods of instruction, with classical texts being taught in alignment with India’s rich oral and written traditions.

Currently, the Faculty encompasses eight departments and one centre, offering instruction in 23 subjects. It provides courses at the Shastri (Undergraduate) and Acharya (Postgraduate) levels across eight disciplines, alongside Vidyavaridhi (Ph.D.) programs in Sanskrit, Theology, and traditional subjects. Additionally, it offers several diploma and certificate courses.

The Faculty publishes an annual research journal, Sanskritvidya, which serves as a platform for scholars of
Oriental sciences. Furthermore, it has consistently published the Vishwapanchang since 1926 CE, continuing a legacy of scholarly contribution.

The Faculty of Sanskrit Vidya Dharm Vigyan (SVDV) at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) stands as a beacon of traditional Indian knowledge and wisdom. It has continued to uphold its mission of promoting the study of
Sanskrit, ancient Indian scriptures, and Dharmic studies. The academic year 2023-24 saw the Faculty engage in a variety of scholarly pursuits, student -centric activities, and collaborations that reflect its dedication to both preserving and advancing India's cultural heritage.

SECTION -9

FACULTY OF SOCIAL SCIENCE

The Faculty of Social Sciences at Banaras Hindu University, one of the oldest and most distinguished centres of learning, has a long tradition of strengthening the academic foundation of the University. Established in 1971, following its separation from the Faculty of Arts (formerly Central Hindu College), the Faculty consists of five departments: Economics, History, Political Science, Psychology, and Sociology. It also includes five specialized centres: the Malviya Centre for Peace Research, Centre for Nepal Studies, Integrated Rural Development Centre,
Centre for Women’s Studies and Development, and the Centre for Social Exclusion and Discrimination.
Additionally, the Faculty hosts two prestigious academic chairs: the Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Chair and the recently established Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyay Chair.

Over the years, the Faculty has trained numerous scholars and researchers, both national and international, whose contributions are recognized and acclaimed globally. In addition to undergraduate and postgraduate education, the Faculty is renowned for its rigorous doctoral research programs. Alongside its core disciplines in the social sciences, the Faculty emphasizes interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary research. It offers a wide range of academic programs, including Bachelor of Arts (B.A.), Master of Arts (M.A.), Post -Graduate Diplomas, and
Ph.D. degrees. Known for its exceptional academic environment, the Faculty is equally committed to student - cantered initiatives and extracurricular activities, fostering the holistic development of its students.

The Faculty of Social Sciences at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) has been at the forefront of academic excellence since its establishment. In the academic year 2023-24, the Faculty continued to uphold its legacy through an array of notable achievements in research, faculty contributions, student-centric activities, and outreach programs.

SECTION 10

FACULTY OF VISUAL ARTS

The Faculty of Visual Arts, established in 1950 at Banaras Hindu University, stands as a distinguished institution renowned for its contributions to the field of art education in India. Comprising three departments and three specialized sections, the Faculty offers a comprehensive range of academic programs, including Bachelor of Fine
Arts (BFA), Master of Fine Arts (MFA), and doctoral (Ph.D.) degrees in Fine Arts. These programs provide specialized training in Applied Art, Painting, Textile Design, Plastic Art (Sculpture), and Pottery Ceramics.
Additionally, the Faculty offers Diploma and Certificate courses, with durations of one year, six months, and two months, catering to a diverse set of learners and artistic disciplines.

A balanced integration of theory and practice defines the curriculum of the Faculty. Essential theoretical subjects, particularly in the History of Visual Arts and Design, complement the practical focus of both BFA and MFA programs, enriching students' understanding of artistic traditions and contemporary practices. The Faculty boasts two state-of-the-art exhibition galleries, which host curated shows from renowned artists, emerging talents, and students from across India, providing a dynamic platform for artistic expression and cultural dialogue.

Attracting students from all over India and abroad, the Faculty of Visual Arts serves as a vibrant hub for creative minds. Its alumni go on to forge successful careers in various artistic professions, excelling as professional freelancers, educators, and industry leaders both within India and on the international stage. The legacy of the
Faculty continues to thrive, making it a beacon of excellence in the visual arts education landscape.

The Faculty of Visual Arts at Banaras Hindu University has had a remarkable academic year (2023 -24), characterized by numerous achievements in research, artistic exhibitions, collaborations, and student -focused activities. This report outlines these accomplishments and provides a detailed analysis of the department’s contribution to the academic and creative fields.

MASTER OF FINE ARTS

Admission in Master of Fine Arts in (i) Painting, (ii) Applied Arts, (iii) Plastic Arts, (iv) Pottery & Ceramics, (v)
Textile Design having CUET and Practical Examination as assessment components of entrance examination.
1. For admission to the above Masters in Fine Arts (MFA) courses, a candidate would be required to appear in
CUET and Practical Test. The practical test would include *Portfolio and Original Work presentation (Panel
Evaluation consisting of External and Internal for 200 marks) and interview (Panel Evaluation consisting of
External and Internal for 200 marks) by a committee to be constituted by the BHU. The Practical Test shall be of 400 marks. A candidate will be considered to have appeared in the Common University Entrance Test conducted by the NTA for any of the above MFA course only if he/ she has appeared in the Theory (CUET) as well as in Practical Test.

2. No Scrutiny/Re-evaluation of Answer sheet of practical test will be done at any stage.

3. *Portfolio review and interview: The candidates who have secured more than the prescribed cut-off marks limit in Theory Paper will be required to submit: A digital Portfolio of 8-10 image of the subject concerned
(Applied Art, Painting, Plastic Art, Pottery Ceramic and Textile Design); Artwork (A-4 Size, PDF Format, executed during the course of BFA duly verified and authenticated by the Head of the Department of the candidate’s department. Each image in the portfolio should include the candidates Entrance Exam Roll No.,
Title, Year made in, Medium and Size/Dimension in cm.

4. Candidates numbering Seven times the intake for MFA courses course in each category drawn on the basis of merit of Entrance test conducted by NTA will be called to appear in the Practical Test at Varanasi Centre only. In these courses marks obtained/rank in the Entrance Test (CUET) would not be disclosed till the
Practical Test component is over. University will declare a list of shortlisted candidates in each category who qualify for the Practical Test without disclosing their test scores.

5. During the Practical Examinations, the shortlisted candidates will be required to submit their portfolio and three original works, attested by their Institution/Department, to the concerned departments of the Faculty of Visual Arts.

6. In case of doubt on the submitted portfolio and three original works by the applicant, a skill test may be taken by the panel of experts during the practical examination.

7. Appearance in both Theory and Practical (Portfolio and Original Work Examinations) is mandatory in order to be eligible for consideration for admission.

8. For MFA, minimum qualifying marks for theory paper will be 35% and in the practical minimum qualifying marks will be 45%. The University reserves the right to modify the above minimum qualifying marks. If the
University decides to lower down the minimum qualifying marks of 35% prescribed for theory component
(CBT) of MPA course, then the merit will be computed as follows:

(i) Firstly those candidates will be put in the merit list according to their combined marks in theory (CBT) and practical tests who have secured the minimum qualifying marks in the theory as well as practical;

(ii) After that those candidates will be put in the merit list on the basis of their combined marks in theory
(CBT) and practical tests who have obtained the minimum qualifying marks in the practical test but could not get minimum qualifying marks in theory.

In case of MFA, the above procedure will be applicable for candidates of all categories. Further, a candidate will be considered deemed appeared in the CUET PG conducted by NTA who appeared in the Theory as well as
Practical(s).

                                               THE UNIVERSITY AT A GLANCE
  Banaras Hindu University (BHU), stands as one of the most prestigious and historic educational institutions in
  the country. Founded in 1916 by the visionary nationalist leader Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, BHU was
  established with the mission of promoting Indian culture, spirituality, and values through modern scientific
  education. Its holistic model of education, conceived and enriched by its illustrious founder, offers refreshingly
  new perspectives to young minds, and nurtures and facilitates their creative talents as well. This unique blend
  of  traditional  and  contemporary  knowledge  systems  has  positioned  BHU  as  a  beacon  of  learning  and
  enlightenment.

  The sprawling campus of BHU, which stretches over 550 Hectares (1,300 acres), is a testament to its grandeur
  and academic excellence. Perhaps this is one of the few universities in the world where courses ranging from
  nursery and primary school to Doctoral/ Post-doctoral degrees are taught and pursued within a walled campus.
  It enshrines within its precincts, a phenomenal range of teaching disciplines incorporating almost all conceivable
  subjects of Physical, Chemical & Biological Sciences, Engineering & Technology, Medical Sciences, Humanities,
  Sanskrit  Vidya Dharm Vigyan  Social  Sciences,  Commerce,  Law,  Education, Visual  Arts,  Performing  Arts,
  Agriculture, Veterinary Sciences, Library Science, Journalism and a large number of Indian and Foreign
  Languages.

  The university houses 5 Institutes, 16 Faculties, 136 Departments, and the Mahila Mahavidyalaya. The Indian
  Institute of Technology (BHU) is also situated on its campus. These institutions contribute to overarching goal
  of the University, fostering interdisciplinary learning and research. The emphasis on research and innovation is
  evident from the state-of-the-art laboratories, libraries, and research centres of the University, which provide
  students and faculty with unparalleled resources to pursue their academic interests.




                                                               Page 9 of 125
 
  The BHU has four colleges admitted to its privileges in the city. The University also runs three schools apart from
  having a Kendriya Vidyalaya within the campus. In addition, the University has its South Campus spread over
  an area of 1092.6 Hectares (2700 acres) located about 75 kms from the main campus, at Barkachha in Mirzapur
  district, Uttar Pradesh.

  The cultural and intellectual vibrancy of BHU is reflected in its diverse student body and faculty, who come from
  various parts of India and the world. This melting pot of cultures and ideas creates a stimulating environment
  that encourages critical thinking, creativity, and holistic development. The university's commitment to inclusivity
  and diversity is further underscored by its numerous scholarships and financial aid programs, which ensure that
  talented students from all socioeconomic backgrounds can access quality education.

  Beyond academics, BHU is celebrated for its active engagement in extracurricular activities and social initiatives.
  The University hosts a multitude of cultural festivals, sports events, and seminars that enrich the student
  experience and foster a sense of community. Additionally, outreach programs and collaborations with national
  and international institutions underscore the role of BHU as a catalyst for societal progress and global
  cooperation.

  2.7 INTER-SE RANKING: Breaking Ties in CUET (PG) - 2026 Merit Scores:

  In case of equal RANK in CUET-PG (for all courses), the following criteria shall be adopted for inter                      -se ranking,
  If two or more candidates have the same score for a program in the CUET (PG) - 2026, the following criteria will
  be used in a stated order to break the tie:

  1.   Qualifying Exam Performance: The candidate with the highest marks in the qualifying degree examination
        shall be given preference. Provided that in case of those students whose final semester/year results have
        not been declared, the qualifying degree examination percentage shall include marks obtained till last
        semesters.
  2.   If the tie persists, the candidate with the higher marks in their last available semester/year final year of the
        qualifying degree will be considered. If a tie remains, the process will move to considering marks in the
        preceding semesters (or years) until the tie is broken.
  3.   Age: If the tie remains, the older candidate (based on their Class X certificate date of birth) will be given
        preference.
  4.   Application Number: If all else is equal, Application number of the candidate; preference will be given to the
        candidate who applied earlier in the CAP         -PG 2026.

                                    3.1 INSTITUTE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES



































  The Institute of Agricultural Sciences (I.Ag.Sc.) at Banaras Hindu University has concluded a distinguished
  journey spanning 93 years, marked by substantial contributions towards alleviating hunger in India. Initially
  established under various names, it was formally designated as the Institute of Agricultural Sciences in 1981,
  with a mission to integrate education, research, extension services, and agricultural development. Pioneering as
  the first Institute of Agricultural Research offering M.Sc. and Ph.D. degrees, it commenced undergraduate
  education in 1945 under the title of the College of Agriculture within the Faculty of Engineering. This college
  attained independent status as the Faculty of Agriculture in 1968.

  Presently, the Institute comprises two faculties: the Faculty of Agriculture and the Faculty of Veterinary and
  Animal Sciences, encompassing 11 and 15 departments respectively along with three auxiliary units. It currently
  provides comprehensive education and involved in research across diverse fields of Agriculture and Veterinary
  Sciences, offering programs such as B.Sc. (Ag.), 02 B.Tech. (DT & FT) programs, 11 M.Sc. (Ag.) programs, 02
  M.Tech ( DT & FPT) programs, B.V.Sc. & A.H., and Ph.D. programs.

  The  academic  year  2023-24  marked  a  period  of  substantial  achievement  and  growth  for  the  institute,
  characterized   by   robust   research   outputs,   strategic   collaborations,   infrastructure   development,   and
  comprehensive student development initiatives. These accomplishments underscore the commitment of the
  Institute to excellence in education, research, and community engagement, positioning it as a leader in
  agricultural and allied sciences.
