  The Institute of Medical Sciences (IMS), a distinguished constituent of Banaras Hindu University, stands as a
  premier medical institution in India, notable for its four comprehensive faculties: the Faculty of Medicine,
  comprising 35 departments; the Faculty of Ayurveda, with 17 departments; the Faculty of Dental Sciences; and
  the College of Nursing. In addition to these faculties, the Institute operates several constituent hospitals, offering
  a total of 2,614 beds, including 1,385 in Sir Sunderlal Hospital, 180 in the Ayurveda Wing, 334 in the Trauma
  Centre, 13 in the Faculty of Dental Sciences, 430 in the Centenary Super Specialty Block, 100 in the Mother &
  Child Health Wing, 60 in the        Centre of Excellence for Mental Health, 12 in the Bone                Marrow Transplant & Stem
  Cell Research Centre, and 100 in the Regional Institute of Ophthalmology. IMS also houses a Regional Resource
  Centre for Telemedicine, providing state-of-the-art tele-education and tele-consultation facilities with high-tech
  classrooms.

  The Institute offers comprehensive academic programs in medicine, including undergraduate (UG), postgraduate
  (PG), post-doctoral (D.M. and M.Ch.), and Ph.D. degrees, fostering cutting-edge research, clinical training, and
  medical practice in a wide array of disciplines.

  Hospitals and Clinical Facilities

  With 1,585 beds in Sir Sunderlal Hospital and 334 beds in the Trauma Centre, IMS extends world-class healthcare
  services to economically disadvantaged            populations    from Eastern Uttar Pradesh, seven neighbouring              states, and
  even the adjoining country of Nepal. In addition to these facilities, IMS maintains a Staff Health Centre and a
  Student Health Care Complex, ensuring quality medical services for the staff and students of the University.

  IMS is currently undergoing a major transformation, aspiring to become an institution of excellence akin to the
  All-India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS). As part of this upgrade, a 430                    -bed Centenary Super        -Specialty
  Block has been established, offering highly advanced and specialized medical care. This state                         -ofthe-art facility
  is equipped with 13 modular operating theatres, 50 Intensive Care Units (ICUs), and 19 Critical Care Units
  (CCUs), covering 11 major super             -specialty disciplines. The block also features a modern blood bank with
  component separation facilities, which has received an 'A' grade rating from NACO, New Delhi. A mobile blood
  bank van further enhances patient care services.

  Additionally, several new healthcare facilities have been inaugurated, including a 100                        -bed Mother and Child
  Health Wing, a 100       -bed Regional Institute of Ophthalmology, a 12              -bed Bone Marrow Transplant & Stem Cell
  Research Centre, and a 60-bed Centre of Excellence for Mental Health. These units, inaugurated by Honourable
  Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, are now fully operational.

  Trauma Centre

  The Trauma Centre of IMS is the largest of its kind in India, housing 334 beds, including a 27-bed modern ICU.
  The facility is centrally air-conditioned and equipped with centralized gas and vacuum distribution, supported by
  a 10,000-liter liquid oxygen plant. The centre features 13 modular operating theatres, as well as extensive

  India, ultimately aspiring to eradicate poverty through the judicious and equitable management of the nation’s
  natural resources.

  The Institute stands as a beacon of interdisciplinary education in the realms of environment and sustainable
  development.  It  offers  a  Master  of  Science  program  in  Environmental  Sciences,  with  specializations  in
  Environmental Biotechnology, Ecological Sciences, and Earth and Atmospheric Sciences, in addition to hosting
  doctoral and integrated       M.Phil.-Ph.D. programs in        various branches of Environmental          Sciences and Technology.
  These include, but are not limited to, Earth and Atmospheric Sciences, Ecological Sciences, Environmental
  Microbiology,    and Sustainable      Agriculture.   The Institute also houses the DST-Mahamana Centre of Excellence in
  Climate Change, an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary collaborative research initiative aligned with India’s
  National Action Plan on Climate Change.

  Beyond its primary mission of teaching and research at the Institute, faculty members contribute to the academic
  community by participating in teaching and mentoring students across various M.Sc. programs, including
  Geophysics, Environmental Sciences, Environmental Sciences & Technology, and Applied Microbiology, both at
  Banaras Hindu University and other national and international institutions.

                                     3.4 INSTITUTE OF MANAGEMENT STUDIES












































  Banaras Hindu University reached a significant milestone in fulfilling the visionary aspirations of its illustrious
  founder by introducing postgraduate and doctoral programs in Management in 1968, establishing a new
  Department within the Faculty of Commerce. Recognizing the growing demand for high-calibre management
  education and research, the University elevated the Department of Management Studies to an independent
  Faculty of Management Studies in 1984. This transformation enabled the institution to offer innovative, industry-
  relevant programs, guided by distinguished faculty members of national and international repute. Further
  advancing its commitment to excellence, the Faculty was upgraded to the Institute of Management Studies in
  December 2015.

  The Institute now offers a comprehensive suite of academic programs, including the MBA, MBA                                 -IB, MBA
  (Agribusiness),

  Ph.D. in Management Studies, as well as various diploma and certificate programs. The Institute maintains robust
  connections with the corporate sector, with academic collaborations and Guest lectures from industry experts
  play a crucial role in enhancing the teaching-learning experience. These interactions, along with valuable insights
  from industry leaders, inform the curriculum revision process, ensuring that the programs remain relevant and
  cutting-edge.

  Moreover, the Institute houses a Business Clinic, designed to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and
  practical application. The Clinic extends learning beyond the classroom, offering expert services to entrepreneurs
  and business entities.

  The Atal Incubation Centre        —Mahamana Foundation for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (AIC                      -MFIE-IM-BHU)
  operates within the Institute of Management Studies. As one of the flagship initiatives under the Atal Innovation
  Mission, supported by NITI Aayog, Government of India, this Centre fosters innovative startups, guiding them
  towards becoming scalable and sustainable enterprises.

  The academic year 2023-24 was a period of substantial achievement for the Institute of Management Studies
  (IMS)  at  BHU.  The  institute  demonstrated  excellence  in  various  domains,  including  research,  strategic
  collaborations,  infrastructure  development,  student            -centric  activities,  and  placement  outcomes.  These
  accomplishments reflect the unwavering commitment of the Institute to quality education, innovation, and
  community engagement, further solidifying its status as a leading institution in management studies.

                                                     5.1 FACULTY OF ARTS
































  The Faculty of Arts at Banaras Hindu University, originally established as a center of humanities, traces its roots
  to the Central Hindu College, founded by Dr. Annie Besant in 1898. This institution laid the groundwork for what
  would become the prestigious Banaras Hindu University (BHU), a beacon of academic excellence with a promising
  future. The Faculty is envisioned as a hub for preserving and promoting the rich intellectual and cultural heritage
  of India, fostering a harmonious blend of traditional and modern knowledge systems.

  The Faculty of Arts continually strives to nurture a unique symbiosis between time honoured wisdom and
  contemporary ideas, with the goal of advancing the holistic development of humanity. It maintains a dynamic
  academic  environment  that encourages  interdisciplinary research  and  innovation,  all  while  upholding  the
  principles of human liberty. Through its 21 departments and 4 significant research centers, the Faculty promotes
  rigorous dialogues on traditional and indigenous knowledge systems, evaluating their relevance and significance
  in today's world.

  The Faculty offers a comprehensive range of undergraduate, postgraduate, and research programs in disciplines
  such as Indian and foreign languages, history, culture, archaeology, art history, and philosophy and religion.
  Additionally, it provides a variety of professional and vocational courses, including Journalism and Mass
  Communication, Library and Information Science, Tourism and Travel Management, Museology, and Functional
  Hindi. With its B.A., M.A. programs in 21 disciplines, Ph.D. opportunities, and a wide array of diploma and
  certificate courses, the Faculty is dedicated to shaping informed and culturally aware citizens capable of
  contributing meaningfully to society.

  The Faculty of Arts at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) has showcased an impressive range of academic
  achievements, research initiatives, and extracurricular activities during the academic year 2023                     -2024.

                                                    5.2 FACULTY OF COMMERCE








































  The Faculty of Commerce at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) is recognized as one of the largest commerce
  faculties in India, with a rich history dating back to 1940. Initially established as an adjunct department to the
  Department of Economics, it gained independence during the University’s Silver Jubilee celebrations in 1950 and
  was later elevated to the status of a full-fledged faculty in 1965.

  In the current academic year, the Faculty of Commerce at BHU continues to provide a diverse array of programs,
  including B.Com. (Honours), M.Com., and Ph.D. courses. Additionally, it offers specialized programs such as the
  M.B.A. in Financial Management (M.B.A.            -F.M.), M.B.A. in Risk & Insurance (M.B.A.          -R&I), and M.B.A. in Foreign
  Trade (M.B.A.    -F.T.) on a self  -financing basis, catering to the evolving needs of the business world.

  The Faculty's reach extends to the Rajiv Gandhi South Campus (RGSC) in Barkachha, Mirzapur, where it offers
  B.Com. (Honours)       under a    paid seat category and       B.Com. (Honours)       in Financial Market Management (F.M.M.).
  This expansion provides students in the region with opportunities for specialized education in commerce and
  finance.

  The faculty’s accomplishments during this period illustrate its active engagement in research, publication, and
  academic collaboration. The contributions in research publications, book authorship, and chapter writing have
  enriched the academic landscape, while active participation in conferences and seminars has helped to further
  the exchange of knowledge. These achievements highlight the Faculty’s ongoing commitment to academic
  excellence and its role as a vital contributor to scholarly advancements at both national and international levels.

                                               5.3 FACULTY OF EDUCATION
































  Faculty of Education, Banaras Hindu University is committed to promote education by providing educators with
  the tools and strategies needed to teach all learners, regardless of their abilities, and integrating inclusive
  education practices within the broader educational framework. The faculty encourages innovation by fostering
  the development and application of advanced teaching strategies, digital technologies, and inclusive curricula
  that cater to the needs of all students. With a focus on research excellence, the faculty leads pioneering research
  in all areas of education, contributing to the academic and practical knowledge required to enhance educational
  practices in diverse classrooms. Additionally, the Faculty aims to develop strong leadership in education,
  preparing future leaders who are equipped to manage educational institutions, advocate for inclusive policies,
  and drive reforms that will transform the education sector.

  Program Offered:
  The faculty of Education has six programme in the area of education and special education. The B.Ed. (Bachelor
  of Education), M.Ed. (Master of Education) and M.A. (Master of Arts in Education) programs at Banaras Hindu
  University (BHU) are recognized by the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE). NCTE is the national
  regulatory body for teacher education in India, ensuring that the curriculum, teaching methods, and faculty
  standards meet the requirements for quality education and              professional development of educators. In addition,
  the B.Ed. in Special Education (Hearing Impairment and Visual Impairment) and M.Ed. Special Education (Visual
  Impairment) programs are recognized by the Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI), New Delhi ensuring that the
  programs align with the standards for special education and equip graduates to work effectively with students
  with disabilities, particularly those with hearing and visual impairments.
  ⮲   B.Ed. (Bachelor of Education): A comprehensive program preparing educators for diverse educational
       environments with a focus on teaching practices.
  ⮲   M.Ed. (Master of Education): A program designed to deepen the knowledge and skills of educators in
       teaching, leadership, curriculum design, and educational research.
  ⮲   M.A. Education (Master of Arts in Education): A program designed to deepen the knowledge and skills of
       educators in teaching, leadership, curriculum design, and educational research.
  ⮲   B.Ed. (Special Education - Hearing Impairment): A specialized undergraduate program designed to prepare
       teachers to work effectively with students who have hearing impairments. Emphasizes inclusive teaching,
       assistive technology, and rehabilitative practices.
  ⮲   B.Ed. (Special Education       - Visual Impairment): A specialized undergraduate program designed to prepare
       teachers to work effectively with students who have visual impairments. Emphasizes inclusive teaching,
       assistive technology, and rehabilitative practices.
  ⮲    M.Ed. (Special Education - Visual Impairment): A program tailored for individuals seeking specialized training
       in the education of students with visual impairments. Focuses on rehabilitation, advocacy, and inclusive
       education strategies.

  violin, flute, tabla and mridangam), and classical dance forms such as Kathak and Bharatnatyam.

                                 FACULTY OF SANSKRIT VIDYA DHARMA VIJNANA
































  The Faculty of Sanskrit Vidya Dharm Vigyan, established in 1918, was founded with the dual purpose of
  preserving and advancing the study of ancient Indian scriptures, Sanskrit language, and literature, while fostering
  a meaningful dialogue between Eastern and Western traditions. Initially known as the Faculty of Prachya Vidya,
  one of its primary aims is to challenge and dispel unfounded misconceptions surrounding Hindu religion,
  spirituality, astrology, and Tantra. It is equally dedicated to restoring the fundamental values of morality and
  religion, contributing to the upliftment of society at large and particularly focusing on the well                      -being of the
  masses. The Faculty preserves traditional methods              of instruction, with classical texts being taught in alignment
  with India’s rich oral and written traditions.

  Currently, the Faculty encompasses eight departments and one centre, offering instruction in 23 subjects. It
  provides courses at the Shastri (Undergraduate) and Acharya (Postgraduate) levels across eight disciplines,
  alongside Vidyavaridhi (Ph.D.) programs in Sanskrit, Theology, and traditional subjects. Additionally, it offers
  several diploma and certificate courses.

  The Faculty publishes an annual research journal, Sanskritvidya, which serves as a platform for scholars of
  Oriental sciences. Furthermore, it has consistently published the Vishwapanchang since 1926 CE, continuing a
  legacy of scholarly contribution.

  The Faculty of Sanskrit Vidya Dharm Vigyan (SVDV) at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) stands as a beacon of
  traditional Indian knowledge and wisdom. It has continued to uphold its mission of promoting the study of
  Sanskrit, ancient Indian scriptures, and Dharmic studies. The academic year 2023-24 saw the Faculty engage in
  a variety of scholarly pursuits, student        -centric activities, and collaborations that reflect its dedication to both
  preserving and advancing India's cultural heritage.

                                                FACULTY OF SOCIAL SCIENCE































  The Faculty of Social Sciences at Banaras Hindu University, one of the oldest and most distinguished centres of
  learning, has a long tradition of strengthening the academic foundation of the University. Established in 1971,
  following its separation from the Faculty of Arts (formerly Central Hindu College), the Faculty consists of five
  departments: Economics, History, Political Science, Psychology, and Sociology. It also includes five specialized
  centres: the Malviya Centre for Peace Research, Centre for Nepal Studies, Integrated Rural Development Centre,
  Centre  for  Women’s  Studies  and  Development,  and  the  Centre  for  Social  Exclusion  and  Discrimination.
  Additionally, the Faculty hosts two prestigious academic chairs: the Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Chair and the recently
  established Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyay Chair.

  Over the years, the Faculty has trained numerous scholars and researchers, both national and international,
  whose contributions are recognized and acclaimed globally. In addition to undergraduate and postgraduate
  education, the Faculty is renowned for its rigorous doctoral research programs. Alongside its core disciplines in
  the social sciences, the Faculty emphasizes interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary research. It offers a wide range
  of academic programs, including Bachelor of Arts (B.A.), Master of Arts (M.A.), Post                      -Graduate Diplomas, and
  Ph.D. degrees. Known for its exceptional academic environment, the Faculty is equally committed to student                              -
  cantered initiatives and extracurricular activities, fostering the holistic development of its students.

  The Faculty of Social Sciences at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) has been at the forefront of academic excellence
  since its establishment. In the academic year 2023-24, the Faculty continued to uphold its legacy through an
  array of notable achievements in research, faculty contributions, student-centric activities, and outreach
  programs.

                                                     FACULTY      OF VISUAL ARTS



































  The Faculty of Visual Arts, established in 1950 at Banaras Hindu University, stands as a distinguished institution
  renowned for its contributions to the field of art education in India. Comprising three departments and three
  specialized sections, the Faculty offers a comprehensive range of academic programs, including Bachelor of Fine
  Arts (BFA), Master of Fine Arts (MFA), and doctoral (Ph.D.) degrees in Fine Arts. These programs provide
  specialized training in Applied Art, Painting, Textile Design, Plastic Art (Sculpture), and Pottery Ceramics.
  Additionally, the Faculty offers Diploma and Certificate courses, with durations of one year, six months, and two
  months, catering to a diverse set of learners and artistic disciplines.

  A balanced integration of theory and practice defines the curriculum of the Faculty. Essential theoretical subjects,
  particularly in the History of Visual Arts and Design, complement the practical focus of both BFA and MFA
  programs, enriching students' understanding of artistic traditions and contemporary practices. The Faculty boasts
  two state-of-the-art exhibition galleries, which host curated shows from renowned artists, emerging talents, and
  students from across India, providing a dynamic platform for artistic expression and cultural dialogue.

  Attracting students from all over India and abroad, the Faculty of Visual Arts serves as a vibrant hub for creative
  minds. Its alumni go on to forge successful careers in various artistic professions, excelling as professional
  freelancers, educators, and industry leaders both within India and on the international stage. The legacy of the
  Faculty continues to thrive, making it a beacon of excellence in the visual arts education landscape.

  The Faculty of Visual Arts at Banaras Hindu University has had a remarkable academic year (2023                                     -24),
  characterized by numerous achievements in research, artistic exhibitions, collaborations, and student                           -focused
  activities. This report outlines these accomplishments and provides a detailed analysis of the department’s
  contribution to the academic and creative fields.

                                                       MASTER       OF FINE ARTS

  Admission in Master of Fine Arts in (i) Painting, (ii) Applied Arts, (iii) Plastic Arts, (iv) Pottery & Ceramics, (v)
  Textile Design having CUET and Practical Examination as assessment components of entrance examination.
  1.   For admission to the above Masters in Fine Arts (MFA) courses, a candidate would be required to appear in
        CUET and Practical Test. The practical test would include *Portfolio and Original Work presentation (Panel
        Evaluation consisting of External and Internal for 200 marks) and interview (Panel Evaluation consisting of
        External and Internal for 200 marks) by a committee to be constituted by the BHU. The Practical Test shall
        be of 400 marks. A candidate will be considered to have appeared in the Common University Entrance Test
        conducted by the NTA for any of the above MFA course only if he/ she has appeared in the Theory (CUET)
        as well as in Practical Test.

  2.   No Scrutiny/Re-evaluation of Answer sheet of practical test will be done at any stage.

  3.   *Portfolio review and interview: The candidates who have secured more than the prescribed cut-off marks
        limit in Theory Paper will be required to submit: A digital Portfolio of 8-10 image of the subject concerned
        (Applied Art, Painting, Plastic Art, Pottery Ceramic and Textile Design); Artwork (A-4 Size, PDF Format,
        executed during the course of BFA duly verified and authenticated by the Head of the Department of the
        candidate’s department. Each image in the portfolio should include the candidates Entrance Exam Roll No.,
        Title, Year made in, Medium and Size/Dimension in cm.

  4.   Candidates numbering Seven times the intake for MFA courses course in each category drawn on the basis
        of merit of Entrance test conducted by NTA will be called to appear in the Practical Test at Varanasi Centre
        only. In these courses marks obtained/rank in the Entrance Test (CUET) would not be disclosed till the
        Practical Test component is over. University will declare a list of shortlisted candidates in each category who
        qualify for the Practical Test without disclosing their test scores.

  5.   During the Practical Examinations, the shortlisted candidates will be required to submit their portfolio and
        three original works, attested by their Institution/Department, to the concerned departments of the Faculty
        of Visual Arts.

  6.   In case of doubt on the submitted portfolio and three original works by the applicant, a skill test may be
        taken by the panel of experts during the practical examination.

  7.   Appearance in both Theory and Practical (Portfolio and Original Work Examinations) is mandatory in order
        to be eligible for consideration for admission.

  8.   For MFA, minimum qualifying marks for theory paper will be 35% and in the practical minimum qualifying
        marks will be 45%. The University reserves the right to modify the above minimum qualifying marks. If the
        University decides to lower down the minimum qualifying marks of 35% prescribed for theory component
        (CBT) of MPA course, then the merit will be computed as follows:

        (i) Firstly those candidates will be put in the merit list according to their combined marks in theory (CBT)
             and practical tests who have secured the minimum qualifying marks in the theory as well as practical;

        (ii) After that those candidates will be put in the merit list on the basis of their combined marks in theory
             (CBT) and practical tests who have obtained the minimum qualifying marks in the practical test but
             could not get minimum qualifying marks in theory.

  In case of MFA, the above procedure will be applicable for candidates of all categories. Further, a candidate will
  be considered deemed appeared in the CUET PG conducted by NTA who appeared in the Theory as well as
  Practical(s).

INFORMATION BULLETIN 2026

FOR ADMISSION TO UNDERGRADUATE PROGRAM

BACHELOR OF VETERINARY SCIENCE & ANIMAL
HUSBANDRY COURSE
(B.V.Sc.& A.H.)

 at

RAJIV GANDHI SOUTH CAMPUS MIRZAPUR UP.

ACADEMIC SESSION 2026-27

DISCLAIMER

The Banaras Hindu University, Varanasi reserves the right to revise, amend or delete any part of the Information Bulletin 2026 of the Bachelor of Veterinary Science &
Animal Husbandry Course for Admission to Undergraduate Program i.e. B.V.Sc. & A.H. at
RAJIV GANDHI SOUTH CAMPUS MIRZAPURUP without prior notice. Any change so made shall be updated on the admission website of the Banaras Hindu University, Varanasi
(BHU). Any change in allotment rules after the release of the Information Bulletin 2026 document shall become effective from the date it is posted on the admission website https://admission.bhu.ac.in/en/ https://bhuadm.samarth.edu.in/index.php
Every effort has been made to present the genuine, official rendition of the rules, regulations, and pertinent details within this document to the best of our ability.
Nonetheless, it must not be interpreted under any circumstances as a guarantee, whether explicit or implicit, concerning the comprehensiveness and precision of the referenced information.
The BHU wants to make it clear that it is not liable for any loss or damage that may be caused to an individual based on the information provided.
Any errors on the admission website, Information Bulletin 2026 of the Bachelor of
Veterinary Science & Animal Husbandry document may be due to unintentional omissions or other reasons.
This disclaimer applies to all parts of the Information Bulletin 2026, including notifications, corrigendum, amendments, addendums, and regulations posted on the website and attached or contained within.
Regularly visit the admission page of the official BHU website for the latest updates on admissions, guidelines, schedules, and important policies.
Any disagreements or legal issues related to Information Bulletin 2026 admissions will be handled exclusively by the Hon’ble High Court of Allahabad, UP.

BANARAS HINDU UNIVERSITY AT AGLANCE
The Banaras Hindu University (BHU), founded by Mahamana Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya ji in
1916, is one of the most prestigious Central Universities in the country. An autonomous institution of distinction and having the Hon'ble President of India as its Visitor, BHU is the largest residential university in Asia. Being a living embodiment of visionaries such as
Mahamana Malaviya ji, Dr. Annie Besant, and Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, this seat of learning epitomizes a synthesis of ancient wisdom and modern scientific temper. Its holistic model of education, conceived and enriched by its illustrious founder, offers refreshingly new perspectives to young minds and nurtures and facilitates their creative talents.

The Founder's Vision

• "It is my earnest hope and prayer that this centre of life and light, which is coming into existence, will produce students who will not only be intellectually equal to the best of their fellow students in other parts of the world, but will also live a noble life, love their country, and be loyal to the Supreme Ruler."

• "A teaching university would but half perform its function, if it does not seek to develop the heart power of its scholars with the same solicitude with which it develops their brain power. Hence, this university has placed the formation of character in youth as one of its principal objectives. It will seek not merely to turn out men as
Engineers, Scientists, Doctors, Theologians, Merchants, but also as men of high character, probity and honour, whose conduct through life would show that they bear the hallmark of a great university."

The University

This university was conceived as a residential university, keeping in view its objective of complete character development and thorough mentoring of students. Perhaps this is the only university in the world where courses ranging from nursery and primary school up to doctoral/post-doctoral degrees are taught and pursued within a walled campus spread over 550 Hectares (1360 acres) and having majestic buildings of great architectural delight.

It enshrines within its precincts, a phenomenal range of teaching disciplines incorporating almost all conceivable subjects of Science,
Engineering & Technology, Medical Sciences, Humanities, Social Sciences, Commerce, Law,
Education, Visual Arts, Performing Arts, Sanskrit Vidya Dharm Vigyan, Agriculture, Veterinary
Sciences, Library Science, Journalism and a large number of Indian and Foreign Languages.

There are at present 5 departments receiving support under Special Assistance Programme,7UGC-Innovative /TRIEA /Other Programme and 3-DST-FIST (Fund for Improvement of Science
& Technology) 4 departments/schools are supported under FIST programme of DST. It also has four colleges admitted to the privileges of the university which are located in the city. The university also has three schools apart from having a Kendriya Vidyalaya housed in the
Campus.

In addition, the Rajiv Gandhi South Campus has been established in the year 2006 in a sprawling campus of 1092. 6 Hectares (2700 acres) located about 75kms away from the main campus, at Barkachha in Mirzapur district, Uttar Pradesh.

Hall mark of Excellence
In NIRF, Banaras Hindu University has been consistently ranked among the top universities of
India and it has also been recognized as an Institution of Eminence in the country by the
Ministry of Education, a recognition given only to five Public Sector Universities of the nation.

Institute of Agricultural Sciences
Committed to the objectives of holistic, sustainable and equitable development of agriculture and allied sciences, aimed at liberty, security and prosperity through competent human resource development by virtue of integrated approach of teaching, research and extension, determined for creation of knowledge base for the benefit of the farming community, improvement of crops/ vegetables/ fruits/livestock/ poultry/ fish for enhanced input use efficiency & production, and committed for quality seed production and dissemination of proven technologies towards improving livelihood security and realizing the dream of Hunger Free Society, our achievements in Education (including Sports and Cultural activities) and Research (including Extension activities) justify the funds sanctioned, created and generated from time to time.

Institute of Medical Sciences
The Institute of Medical Sciences comprises three faculties, namely,
Faculty of Modern Medicine, Faculty of Ayurveda, and Faculty of
Dental Sciences. It offers medical and paramedical courses at undergraduate and postgraduate levels. Through its hospitals, it caters to the clinical needs of more than 20 crores population hailing from 7 states (UP, Bihar, West Bengal, Jharkhand, Odisha,
Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh) and neighbouring countries like
Nepal and Bhutan. More than 40% of the patients visiting the hospital are from low economic strata.

At present, the hospitals have 2614 beds which includes 1385 -Bed Sir Sunder Lal Hospital; 180Bed Ayurveda Wing; 334-Bed Trauma Centre; 13-Bed Dental Science; 430-Bed Centenary Super

Specialty Block; 100 -Bed Mother & Child Health Wing; 60 -Bed Centre of Excellence for Mental
Health; 12-Bed Bone Marrow Transplant & Stem Cell Research Centre and 100 Bed Regional
Institute of Ophthalmology.

Institute of Environmental and Sustainable Development
A National-level Institute of Environment & Sustainable
Development was established in the year 2010. Recruitment of faculty was done in the year 2011. Using education as a tool to achieve sustainability, the institute aims to cover education for sustainable development. The mission of the Institute is to carry out teaching, research, and extension relevant to India's sustainable development, leading to a future that ends poverty and delivers and sustains efficient and equitable management of the country's natural resources.

Institute of Management Studies
The University started a Post Graduate and doctoral program in
Management in the year 1968 as a Department in the Faculty of
Commerce. Envisaging the increasing need for imparting quality management education and research, the University transformed the Department of Management Studies into an independent Faculty of Management Studies in the year 1984.
Dedicated efforts were made to run innovative and need -based programs for the corporate world under the dynamic leadership of professors of national and international repute. The Faculty has been upgraded to the Institute of Management Studies in
December 2015.

Institute of Science
Established in 1916, the Faculty of Science, which was later upgraded to the Institute of Science as a constituent institute of the University, offers undergraduate and postgraduate courses, besides offering Ph.D. programs and several diploma and certificate courses. The Institute comprises 13 Departments,6
Centres and 2 Interdisciplinary Schools. Equipped with advanced and sophisticated laboratories and research facilities, the institute is marching ahead towards excellence in teaching, learning, and research in almost all domains of basic and applied sciences.

Largest Residential Campus in Asia
Over 35,000 students from all over India and abroad are enrolled in various faculties of the university. The university has more than 72 hostels, with nearly 11000 inmates, with all modern amenities, including internet, for the students. It also has a specially designed
International Student hostel to accommodate a large number of foreign students who study here. It also has 1590 staff quarters and 7 guest houses on the campus.

Library
BHU has a Central Library system having more than 15 lac volumes apart from subscription to more than 15000 online journals, 50000 e-books, databases, and a huge collection of digitized rare manuscripts. It functions in conjunction with a chain of Departmental, Faculty and Institute libraries. In addition, BHU has a fully air-conditioned Cyber Library with a seating capacity of over 200. Newly created air-conditioned
PeriodicalHallprovides60cabinsfortheuseoffacultymembers and research scholars.

ICT Infrastructure
The University (Varanasi & RGSC both) has a Wi-Fi-enabled campus. All the academic and administrative offices are Wi-Fi connected. In addition, the University has a 240-kilometerlong fiber-optic backbone of campus-wide LAN, connecting all academic and administrative buildings as well as hostels with a well-equipped Computer Centre, providing high-end computing and training facilities. The university has been provided three 1 Gbps nodes of
National Knowledge Network (NKN) under NME-ICT. Besides these, more than 100 smart classrooms have been augmented for smoothening the online teaching and learning, especially during the COVID times. The university has switched over to a computer-based entrance test and implemented ERP for executing all administrative and financial work, thereby moving towards a paperless office.

The Temple
The Banaras Hindu University has a temple of Lord Shiva called
Shri Vishwanath Temple. It is situated at the center of the campus. The temple is built with white marble. Its detailed planning was done by Malaviyaji himself. The lush campus of Shri
Vishwanath Temple and the beautiful gardens surrounding it are a delight to the eyes of the visitors. The interior of the temple has a
Shiva Lingam, and verses from Hindu scriptures are inscribed on the walls of the temple with pictorial depiction.

Bharat Kala Bhavan
BHU has a museum of international importance - Bharat Kala
Bhawan, which is a treasure trove of rare art and artefacts. The
Bharat Kala Bhavan has 13 galleries having a collection of more than 1 lakh antique and rare sculptures, miniature paintings,
Rajasthani, Mughal and Pahari paintings, coins, jewelry, precious stones, etc. of immense historic value and a very special literary gallery containing manuscripts of famous authors. It also has a rich library containing rare books.

Rajiv Gandhi South Campus

The Banaras Hindu University has extended its outreach by establishing its South Campus at Barkachhain, Mirzapur district.
The RGSC is being developed as a potential hub of education, training, and entrepreneurship for youth and women, especially those belonging to tribes and weaker sections of society. The campus is being developed by the University with a mission to enrich the lives of the population of the region by extending to them opportunities to engage in life -long learning and to benefit from the result of research.

Faculty of Veterinary and Animal Sciences
Faculty of Veterinary and Animal Sciences was established in the year 2015 with the inception of the idea to have a surge of elite veterinary experts from the world-renowned central university, Banaras Hindu University. With the mission approach veterinary faculty came into existence and started its functioning under Institute of Agricultural Sciences. The Faculty comprises of 15 departments and 2 units (Livestock farm Complex and Teaching Veterinary
Clinical Complex) and it is spread in an area of 126 acres. Presently faculty is having core strength of 60 faculty member’s expertise in different horizon of veterinary profession. All the departments are well versed with modern facilities of teaching and research.

5. RESERVATIONS

(i) Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes:

Seats shall be reserved for Scheduled Caste (15%) and Scheduled Tribe (7.5%) candidates in each Course. Admission against these seats will be made provided the candidate has passed the
Qualifying Examination and appeared in the NEET-2026. Every SC/ST candidate shall have to submit a self-attested copy of the Certificate mentioning that the candidate belongs to SC/ST community. Such certificates shall be subject to verification from the concerned District

Candidates must note that Certificate from any other person/authority shall not be accepted in any case. If the candidate happens to belong to SC or ST, his/her caste/tribe must be listed in the appropriate Govt. of India schedule. The Caste Certificate should clearly state:

                           BANARAS HINDU UNIVERSITY AT AGLANCE
  The Banaras Hindu University (BHU), founded by Mahamana Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya ji in
  1916,  is  one  of  the most  prestigious Central Universities  in the country.  An  autonomous
  institution of distinction and having the Hon'ble President of India as its Visitor, BHU is the
  largest   residential    university  in  Asia   .  Being  a  living  embodiment  of  visionaries  such  as
  Mahamana Malaviya ji, Dr. Annie Besant,                and Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, this seat             of learning
  epitomizes a synthesis of ancient wisdom and modern scientific temper. Its holistic model of
  education,  conceived         and   enriched     by   its  illustrious    founder,    offers  refreshingly  new
  perspectives to young minds and nurtures and facilitates their creative talents.

  The Founder's Vision

   •   "It is my earnest hope and prayer that this centre of life and light, which is coming into
       existence, will produce students who will not only be intellectually equal to the best of
       their fellow students in other parts of the world, but will also live a noble life, love their
       country, and be loyal to the Supreme Ruler."

   •   "A teaching university would but half perform its function, if it does not
       seek  to  develop  the  heart  power  of  its  scholars  with  the  same
       solicitude    with  which  it  develops  their  brain  power.  Hence,  this
       university has placed the formation of character in youth as one of its
       principal  objectives.      It  will  seek  not     merely  to  turn  out  men  as
       Engineers, Scientists, Doctors, Theologians, Merchants, but also as men
       of high character, probity and honour, whose conduct through life
       would show that they bear the hallmark of a great university."

  The University

  This university was conceived as a residential university, keeping in
  view   its objective of complete character development and thorough
  mentoring of students. Perhaps this is the only university in the world
  where  courses  ranging  from  nursery  and  primary  school  up  to
  doctoral/post-doctoral degrees are taught and pursued within a walled
  campus    spread over      550   Hectares    (1360   acres) and having majestic
  buildings of great architectural delight.

  It  enshrines  within  its  precincts,  a  phenomenal  range  of  teaching
  disciplines incorporating almost all conceivable subjects of Science,
  Engineering & Technology, Medical Sciences, Humanities, Social Sciences, Commerce, Law,
  Education, Visual Arts, Performing Arts, Sanskrit Vidya Dharm Vigyan, Agriculture, Veterinary
  Sciences, Library Science, Journalism and a large number of Indian and Foreign Languages.




                                                                                                         Page 3 of 15
 
  There are at present 5 departments receiving support under Special Assistance Programme,7-
  UGC-Innovative /TRIEA /Other Programme and 3-DST-FIST (Fund for Improvement of Science
  & Technology) 4 departments/schools are supported under FIST programme of DST. It also has
  four colleges    admitted to the privileges of the university which are located in the city. The
  university   also   has  three    schools   apart   from   having    a  Kendriya    Vidyalaya     housed    in  the
  Campus.

  In addition,    the   Rajiv  Gandhi    South    Campus     has  been    established    in  the  year   2006    in a
  sprawling campus of 1092. 6 Hectares (2700 acres) located about 75kms away from the main
  campus, at Barkachha in Mirzapur district, Uttar Pradesh.

  Hall mark of Excellence
  In NIRF, Banaras Hindu University has been consistently ranked among the top universities of
  India  and   it has  also   been   recognized     as  an  Institution   of  Eminence     in  the  country    by  the
  Ministry of Education, a recognition given only to five Public Sector Universities of the nation.

  Institute of Agricultural Sciences
  Committed to the objectives of holistic, sustainable and equitable
  development of       agriculture and allied sciences, aimed at liberty,
  security   and   prosperity   through   competent   human   resource
  development by virtue of integrated approach of teaching, research
  and extension, determined for creation of knowledge base for the
  benefit   of   the   farming   community,   improvement   of   crops/
  vegetables/ fruits/livestock/ poultry/ fish for enhanced input use
  efficiency & production, and committed for quality seed production
  and   dissemination   of   proven   technologies   towards   improving
  livelihood security and realizing the dream of Hunger Free Society,
  our  achievements  in  Education  (including  Sports  and  Cultural
  activities) and Research (including Extension activities) justify the
  funds sanctioned, created and generated from time to time.

  Institute of Medical Sciences
  The Institute of Medical Sciences comprises three faculties, namely,
  Faculty of Modern Medicine, Faculty of Ayurveda, and Faculty of
  Dental  Sciences.  It  offers  medical  and  paramedical  courses  at
  undergraduate  and  postgraduate  levels.  Through  its  hospitals,  it
  caters to the clinical needs of more than 20 crores population hailing
  from   7   states   (UP,   Bihar,   West   Bengal,   Jharkhand,   Odisha,
  Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh) and neighbouring countries like
  Nepal and Bhutan. More than 40% of the patients visiting               the hospital
  are from low economic strata.

  At present, the hospitals have 2614 beds which includes 1385                -Bed Sir Sunder Lal Hospital; 180-
  Bed Ayurveda Wing; 334-Bed Trauma Centre; 13-Bed Dental Science; 430-Bed Centenary Super
                                                                                                         Page 4 of 15
 
  Specialty Block; 100    -Bed Mother & Child Health Wing; 60           -Bed Centre of Excellence for Mental
  Health; 12-Bed Bone Marrow Transplant & Stem Cell Research Centre and 100 Bed Regional
  Institute of Ophthalmology.

  Institute of Environmental and Sustainable Development
  A   National-level   Institute   of   Environment   &   Sustainable
  Development was established in the year 2010. Recruitment of
  faculty was done in the year 2011. Using education as a tool to
  achieve sustainability, the institute aims to cover education for
  sustainable development. The mission of the Institute is to carry
  out  teaching,  research,  and  extension  relevant  to  India's
  sustainable development, leading to a future that ends poverty
  and delivers and sustains efficient and equitable management of
  the country's natural resources.

  Institute of Management Studies
  The University started      a Post Graduate and doctoral program in
  Management in the year 1968 as a Department in the Faculty of
  Commerce. Envisaging the increasing need for imparting quality
  management    education    and    research,    the    University
  transformed  the  Department  of  Management  Studies  into  an
  independent Faculty of Management Studies in the                  year 1984.
  Dedicated efforts were made to run innovative and need                 -based
  programs for the corporate world under the dynamic leadership
  of professors of national and international repute            . The Faculty
  has been upgraded to the          Institute of Management Studies in
  December 2015.

  Institute of Science
  Established in 1916, the Faculty of Science             , which was later
  upgraded to the Institute of Science as a constituent institute of
  the University, offers undergraduate and postgraduate courses,
  besides  offering  Ph.D.  programs  and  several  diploma  and
  certificate courses.     The Institute comprises 13 Departments              ,6
  Centres and 2 Interdisciplinary Schools.         Equipped with advanced
  and  sophisticated  laboratories  and  research  facilities,  the
  institute  is  marching  ahead  towards  excellence  in  teaching,
  learning, and research in almost all domains of basic            and applied
  sciences.






                                                                                                        Page 5 of 15
 
  Largest Residential Campus in Asia
  Over 35,000 students from all over India and abroad are enrolled in various faculties of the
  university. The university has more than 72 hostels,                with nearly 11000 inmates, with all
  modern amenities, including internet,             for the students. It also has a specially designed
  International Student      hostel to accommodate a large number of foreign students who study
  here. It also has 1590 staff quarters and 7 guest houses on the campus.


  Library
  BHU  has  a  Central  Library  system  having  more  than  15              lac
  volumes  apart  from  subscription  to  more  than  15000  online
  journals, 50000 e-books, databases, and a huge collection of
  digitized   rare manuscripts. It functions in conjunction with a
  chain  of  Departmental,  Faculty  and  Institute  libraries.  In
  addition, BHU has a fully air-conditioned Cyber Library with a
  seating  capacity  of  over  200.  Newly  created  air-conditioned
  PeriodicalHallprovides60cabinsfortheuseoffacultymembers    and
  research scholars.


  ICT Infrastructure
  The University (Varanasi & RGSC both) has a Wi-Fi-enabled                    campus. All the academic and
  administrative offices are Wi-Fi connected. In addition, the University has                    a 240-kilometer-
  long fiber-optic backbone of campus-wide LAN, connecting all academic and administrative
  buildings  as  well  as  hostels  with  a  well-equipped  Computer  Centre,  providing  high-end
  computing and training facilities. The university has been provided three 1 Gbps nodes of
  National  Knowledge  Network  (NKN)  under  NME-ICT.  Besides  these,  more  than  100  smart
  classrooms have been augmented for smoothening the online teaching and learning, especially
  during the COVID times. The university has switched over to a computer-based entrance test
  and implemented ERP for executing all administrative and financial work, thereby moving
  towards a paperless office.

  The Temple
  The Banaras     Hindu   University    has  a  temple of    Lord   Shiva   called
  Shri  Vishwanath      Temple.     It  is  situated  at  the  center  of  the
  campus.     The  temple  is  built  with  white  marble.  Its  detailed
  planning was done by Malaviyaji himself. The lush campus of Shri
  Vishwanath Temple and the beautiful gardens surrounding it are a
  delight to the eyes of the visitors. The interior of the temple has a
  Shiva Lingam, and verses from Hindu scriptures are inscribed on
  the walls of the temple with pictorial depiction.
                                                                                                        Page6of15
 
  Bharat Kala Bhavan
  BHU  has  a  museum  of  international  importance              -  Bharat  Kala
  Bhawan, which is a treasure trove of rare art and artefacts. The
  Bharat Kala Bhavan has 13 galleries having a collection of more
  than  1  lakh  antique  and  rare  sculptures,  miniature  paintings,
  Rajasthani, Mughal and Pahari paintings, coins, jewelry, precious
  stones, etc. of immense historic value and a very special literary
  gallery containing manuscripts of famous authors. It also has a rich library containing rare
  books.

  Rajiv Gandhi South Campus

  The  Banaras  Hindu  University  has  extended  its  outreach  by
  establishing    its South   Campus at Barkachhain, Mirzapur district             .
  The RGSC is being developed as a potential hub of education,
  training, and entrepreneurship for youth and women, especially
  those  belonging  to tribes  and weaker  sections of society               .  The
  campus is being developed by the University with a mission to
  enrich the lives of     the population of the region by extending to
  them opportunities to engage in life          -long learning and to benefit
  from the result of research.

  Faculty of Veterinary and Animal Sciences
  Faculty of Veterinary and Animal Sciences was established in the year 2015 with the inception
  of the idea to have a surge of elite veterinary experts from the world-renowned central
  university, Banaras Hindu University. With the mission approach veterinary faculty came into
  existence    and started its functioning under Institute of Agricultural Sciences. The Faculty
  comprises of 15 departments and 2 units (Livestock farm Complex and Teaching Veterinary
  Clinical Complex) and it is spread in an area of 126 acres. Presently faculty is having core
  strength of 60 faculty member’s expertise in different horizon of veterinary profession. All the
  departments are well versed with modern facilities of teaching and research.

 he/she has filled in and the transaction details of payment of application fee) for their own

Under Graduate Admissions 2026-27
Notification for UG MOP-UP (ONLINE)

1. The university has decided to fill the vacant seats through MOP-UP (Online) round allotment, the process of which would be similar to Spot Round.
2. To calculate the final vacancy for MOP-UP round allotment, the Withdraw option will be disabled from
10.09.2026 11:59 PM till the completion of MOP-UP round allotment process.
3. MOP-UP round shall be applicable for all UG Programs including Practical Test based programs provided that the candidate has appeared in respective Practical Test and has qualified.
4. There will be only ONLINE registration for MOP-UP. The eligible candidates will have to apply online for MOPUP Allotment and fill their preferences on their Samarth Portal Dashboard during 12.09.2026 to 14.09.2026
(05:00 PM). The preferences need to be saved and submitted.
5. The eligible candidates for MOP-UP round allotment will be those who were previously registered for BHU
UG Admissions but currently do not hold any admission seat, in Regular or Spot rounds, for whatsoever reason.
The following will be the eligible candidates for MOP-UP round allotment:
a. The candidates who had cancelled/withdrawn their allotted seat.
b. The candidates who defaulted or did not pay the fee after seat allotment.
c. Waitlisted candidate in Regular and Spot rounds.
d. Candidates who were allotted a seat in the Regular or Spot Round but did not report within the stipulated time.
6. The allotment shall be on the basis of merit, their preference choices and reservation policy.
7. The merit of MOP-UP round allotment will be independent of merit of regular round and spot round allotment and therefore will be incomparable.

IMPORTANT DATES

1. UG Cancellation/Withdrawal will be disabled 10.09.2026 (11:59 PM)
2. Declaration of Vacant seats for MOP-UP Round Allotment 11.09.2026

4. Seat Allotment on Student Portal (Round 1) 15.09.2026
5. Fee Payment Deadline 16.09.2026 (23:59hrs)
6. Seat Allotment for BPA/BFA on Student Portal (Round 1) 16.09.2026

7. Fee Payment Deadline 17.09.2026 (23:59hrs)
8. Seat Allotment Declaration (Round 2) on Samarth Portal 18.09.2026

Notice

UG SPOT Round /Mid-Entry Registration & Guidelines

UG Spot Round 2026 will be a mixed round in which new registration will be allowed as Mid-Entry and they will be mixed with the existing applicants for allotment. Candidates interested in applying for admission in the UG
Programs of the Banaras Hindu University through the SPOT Round should note the following:

Activity Date

Spot Round Vacancy List 20.08.2026

Registration of Spot Round (Online) 21.08.2026 - 24.08.2026

Spot Round 1st Allocation 25.08.2026

Spot Round 2nd Allocation 29.08.2026

Eligibility:

1. The following candidates will be eligible to register in the Spot-round:
a. Candidates who have not registered for BHU UG Counselling so far.
b. Candidates who registered for the BHU UG Counselling process but - i. were not offered any seat during the regular round allotment (waitlisted).
ii. were offered seats but could not deposit the fee in stipulated time.
iii. deposited the admission fee but got their admissions withdrawal.
2. Applicants seeking admission in SPOT Round shall have to first register themselves on the Samarth
Portal https://bhucuet.samarth.edu.in/ by paying the SPOT Registration fee Rs. 1000.
3. Candidates already admitted in any regular rounds need not to withdraw for participating in Spot Rounds. They will be considered for allotment / upgrade based on their merit and vacancy in further Spot Rounds.
4. There will be no SPOT Round in courses having practical components i.e. BPA & BFA.
5. The vacant seat status for the Spot Round will be announced on 20.08.2026.
Visit https://admission.bhu.ac.in for “UG Spot Round Vacant Seat Status”.
6. Candidates willing to participate in the SPOT round are advised to ensure themselves regarding the number of seats available in different programs and categories on the counseling portal before registration which is available on the admission tab of BHU website.
7. Seats will be allotted according to the merit and other prevailing rules of the University/GoI against the vacancies shown on the portal for the SPOT round.
8. Cut off of the spot round will be incomparable from the regular rounds.

Chairman
CAC-BHU

                                                                                                      Date: 06.08.2026

                                        BHU CUET – UG Admission 2026
                                                ROUND – 2 Allotment

   Sl. No.                                 Activity                                            Date & Time

      1.       Allocation of Seat and Online Fee Payment Link                       06.08.2026 (08:00 PM)
               (Live on Candidate’s Samarth Dashboard)                                        (Thursday)

      2.       Last Date of Fee Payment                                             08.08.2026 (11:59 PM)
                                                                                             (Saturday)

 Important Note:

    Once the program allotment is released, check them carefully on admission portal dashboard.
     Before making the payment, please ensure that you fulfill all the eligibility criteria for this
     program. It is the responsibility of the candidate to check his/her admission portal and official
     website of BHU regularly after each round of seat allotment.

   The Candidate need to pay the admission fee to secure admission. If a candidate fails to pay the
    admission fee within the Payment Deadline, it will be considered as a cancellation of the allotted
    seat. This means the candidate:

                 will lose the allotted seat.
                 will forfeit all rights associated with the allotted seat.
                 won’t be considered for any further allotment rounds in the same
                  program.

    Candidate may choose either FREEZE or UPGRADE option after payment. If UPGRADE
     option is chosen, the candidate will have to pay the difference in fee. In case of no
     upgradation, the candidate will retain his/her current seat.


 Advice: To avoid any last-minute stress, make sure to pay the admission fee well before the deadline
 and use PC/Laptop for the fee payment.


                                                                                                             Chairman
                                                                                                              CAC-BHU

Post Graduate Admissions 2026-27
Notification for MOP-UP ROUND Allotment

1. The University has decided to fill vacant seats through Mop-Up round allotment, the process of which would be different from Spot Round.
2. To calculate the final vacancy for Mop-Up round allotment, the Withdraw option will be disabled from
03/08/2026 23:59 hrs till the completion of Mop-Up round allotment process.
3. Mop-Up round shall be applicable for all PG courses including GDPI/Practical Test/Physical Test based course provided that the candidate has appeared in respective GDPI/Practical Test/Physical Test and qualified.
4. There will be only ONE round of seat allotment. Therefore there would be no provision for any upgradation.
5. There will be no online registration. The eligible candidates will have to fill Mop-Up Application Form (attached) and report in person at their respective Department/Center on 07/08/2026 between 10:00 AM to 04:00 PM with all relevant documents and BHU PG Registration Form from Samarth Portal.
6. The eligible candidates for Mop-Up round allotment will be those who were registered for BHU PG Admissions
2026-27 but currently do not hold any admission seat, in regular or spot rounds, for whatsoever reason.
The following will be the eligible candidates for Mop-Up round allotment:
a) The candidates who had cancelled/withdrawn their allotted seat.
b) The candidates who did not pay/adjusted fee after seat allotment.
c) The waitlisted candidates in Regular and Spot rounds.
7. The candidates are strongly advised to appear for only ONE programme/course in which he/she had registered previously. In case of multiple applications, the candidature may be cancelled altogether.
8. During physical counseling, the candidate will have to submit a Demand Draft (DD) of ₹2000/- in favour of “The
Registrar, Banaras Hindu University” payable at Varanasi as security deposit.
a) The DD will be returned if the candidate is allotted seat and pay course fee through online portal.
b) The DD will be returned if candidate is not allotted any seat.
Note: It is the responsibility of the candidate to collect the DD from the concerned department after mop up allotment.
c) The DD will be forfeited if candidate is allotted a seat and fails to pay fee.
9. The allotment shall be on the basis of merit, out of the eligible candidates who report in person within stipulated date and time, submit their preference choices and Demand Draft.
10. The merit of Mop-Up round allotment will be independent of merit of regular round and spot round allotment and therefore will be incomparable.
11. Candidates must ensure their eligibility and submit documents accordingly. Missing or incomplete document shall invite cancellation of their candidature.

1. PG Cancellation/Withdrawal will be disabled 03/08/2026 23:59 hrs till the completion of Mop-Up round allotment process
